added.author: AuroraEmiya
added.subject: [BugFix][CI] Remove regex dependency from csrc build cache (#17986)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The csrc cache engine imports third-party `regex` before handling
`snapshot-key`. CI invokes that command before installing project
dependencies, so an environment without `regex` raises
`ModuleNotFoundError`. The restore helper fails open with
`supported=false`; no snapshot key is produced, and persistent L1
restore/save are skipped while the ordinary build can still succeed.

Use Python's standard-library `re` throughout `build_cache.py`, so both
snapshot-key preparation and native-action caching work without
third-party Python packages. Preserve the existing Unicode whitespace
contract by excluding U+001C–U+001F, which stdlib `\s` otherwise
matches. Add a documented, file-specific exception to the repository's
forbidden-import check. Schema remains 4.

The [production A3 producer
log](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/37559987425/job/112595089967)
shows snapshot-key exiting with status 1 before `regex` is installed,
followed by skipped L1 transport. Its captured traceback is not exposed
by the current helper; the missing-dependency failure is reproduced
directly by the new tests.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Local and CI csrc caching no longer requires `regex` to be installed in
the Python interpreter running the cache engine. Cache identity, schema,
artifact layout, and permission/transport behavior are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Reproduced the original failure in an isolated Python environment
without `regex`: direct snapshot-key exits 1, and the real restore
helper returns `supported=false`.
- New tests verify snapshot-key and the real restore helper succeed
before build dependencies are installed.
- A real engine subprocess with `python -I -S` verifies cold MISS/SAVED,
equivalent cross-root warm HIT, and semantic mutation MISS/SAVED. The
warm case does not invoke the test builder.
- Full cache/concurrency/helper suite: **91 passed, 2 skipped**. The two
skipped tests require CMake, which is unavailable in the local WSL
environment.
- Compared the replacement whitespace class with the prior `regex` rule
across all **1,114,112 Unicode code points**: zero differences; added
Unicode boundary regression tests.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks pass at both ordinary and manual stages;
`git diff --check` passes.
- Full-repository pre-commit was attempted. The local ShellCheck binary
segfaults even for `--version`, preventing ShellCheck and
actionlint-with-ShellCheck from completing successfully. This is a local
tooling limitation, not a claimed full-gate pass.
- Production CI L1 cold/warm transport acceptance has not yet been rerun
for this patch.

```bash
python3 -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/ut/_tools \
  tests/ut/_tools/test_build_cache.py \
  tests/ut/_tools/test_build_cache_concurrency.py \
  tests/ut/_tools/test_prepare_csrc_l1_restore.py -q -rs
```

added.author: wzx0726
added.subject: [BugFix][MRV2] Disable EPLB for PCP-only replicated drafts (#17959)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

With MRV2 MTP, a target configured with TP=1, DP=1, PCP>1 and EPLB
enabled creates a replicated draft that executes with PCP=1. The draft
inherits the target's EPLB setting, so reconstructing its configuration
fails:

```text
EPLB requires tensor, prefill-context, or data parallelism, but got TP=1, PCP=1, DP=1
```

Extend the existing replicated-PCP configuration helper to disable EPLB
and clear redundant experts for this draft configuration. Preserve draft
EP and the target's EPLB configuration. The Ascend EPLB controller
checks the draft's existing `enable_eplb` setting before registering it
with the target's EPLB state, and delegates other cases to the upstream
registration path.

Use `dataclasses.replace` for the disabled draft's `EPLBConfig` to copy
declared fields and rerun constructor validation without copying the
target's transient communicator-selection marker. The target retains
that marker for its own initialization.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. For TP=1, DP=1, PCP>1 MRV2 replicated drafts, EPLB is disabled
automatically and a warning is emitted. The draft uses a fixed expert
layout while the target continues load balancing. Draft configurations
with TP>1 or DP>1 retain their existing EPLB behavior. No new
configuration options are introduced.

### How was this patch tested?

For commit `9df7f12cd165c4e5ab86cece94d85269ae0e2c8d`:

- [Full pre-commit checks, including
mypy](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/37725765068/job/113143439770):
passed.
- [Full CPU UT with paired vLLM main commit
`ced6857af`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/37725765068/job/113144868736):
8342 passed, 70 skipped.
- [Full CPU UT with vLLM
`v0.30.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/37725765068/job/113144868693):
8342 passed, 70 skipped.

Regression tests cover the topology boundaries, redundant-expert
clearing, target configuration isolation, inherited draft-loader
reconstruction, and draft registration while preserving target
registration and its async EPLB loop. All seven configuration/loader
regression cases passed on both vLLM versions. The CPU fixture retains
real configuration validation and mocks accelerator availability and
model capability inspection.

NPU startup/inference, accuracy and performance have not been validated
for this commit. NPU CI jobs were skipped because the PR has no
run-enabling label. The [CI
gate](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/37725765068/job/113147485823)
remains failed pending a maintainer adding `ready-precise` or another
supported test label.

added.author: wzx0726
added.subject: [BugFix][MLA] Handle empty PCP prefill ranks (#17972)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

PCP can assign zero real prefill tokens to a rank while retaining padded
KV inputs for collective processing. MLA preprocessing then attempts
`prefill_k_pe.view(0, num_kv_heads, -1)` and raises an ambiguous
zero-element reshape error before prefill attention runs.

Use the existing `self.qk_rope_head_dim` for the last dimension instead
of inferring it. This preserves padded KV processing, collectives,
cropping, and the existing attention path. Add a regression test to the
existing MLA test class for 0, 1, and 3 local tokens, checking that
padded KV input is retained and the returned Q/K/V shapes are correct.
No new flags, state, helpers, or empty-rank early return are introduced.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. MLA PCP requests with a locally empty prefill rank can complete
generation instead of failing during preprocessing. No API or
configuration changes.

### How was this patch tested?

Runtime validation used real BF16 DeepSeek-V2-Lite weights on
Ascend950DT with torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, and CANN 9.1.0.
Configuration: MRV2, TP1/DCP1, PCP1 or PCP2, `enable_mlapo=false`, no
MTP/prefix cache/async scheduling/EP/EPLB, batch token budget 512,
temperature 0, seed 17, and 4 generated tokens.

- **End-to-end empty-rank inference:** with PCP2 and prompt token IDs
`[99297]`, rank0 received 1 real prefill token and rank1 received 0 real
tokens plus 1 padding token. `LLM.generate()` completed and returned
`[254, 4334, 1439, 245]` (`" the difference between a"`) in both
repetitions, matching PCP1. An independent worker trace confirmed the
empty rank in the same inference run; the job exited 0.
- **Negative control:** restoring only the original `-1` reproduced the
first worker exception at `mla_preprocess_prefill`: `cannot reshape
tensor of 0 elements into shape [0, 1, -1] ... ambiguous`. The old-code
job subsequently waited and its own process family was cleaned up; it
did not produce a completed harness result or finish the second planned
repetition.
- **Boundaries and output comparison:** PCP1 and PCP2 eager each
completed lengths 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 32, 513, 514, and 515 twice, with
identical output tokens. Same-PCP2 before/after comparison for lengths
2, 3, 4, 5, and 32 matched exactly. Independent trace runs also
completed a locally empty tail chunk with 512 tokens of prior context
and matched untraced outputs.
- **Graph:** PCP2 `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` completed all nine inputs twice and
matched eager tokens exactly. Both ranks captured token counts `[1, 2]`;
logs confirmed graph replay and 54 FULL executions. This covers eager
prefill plus graph decode. PCP prefill graph (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) is
explicitly unsupported by the current MRV2 PCP implementation.
- **Unit tests:** `pytest -q tests/ut/attention/test_mla_v1.py -k
'prefill or preprocess'` passed all 35 selected tests and exited 0. The
new regression test fails with exit 1 when only the original production
line is restored.
- **Whole-file limitation:** the full MLA test file reported 133
passed/8 failed after the fix versus 132 passed/9 failed with the
original line. The same eight decode/graph-parameter failures were
present in both states; both whole-file jobs timed out during shutdown
after printing their summaries. The whole file is not claimed green.
- **Static checks on this PR branch:** Ruff check, Ruff format check,
AST/source comparison, and `git diff --check` passed. `bash format.sh
ci` could not run its hooks because local `pre-commit` is unavailable.

Runtime evidence was collected on the local MRV2 PCP checkout at
`eb0e37db18cdc3958bdc46113d13f8fabcd25608` with this patch, paired with
vLLM `ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607`. This isolated PR is
based on upstream `0e181fc85fff24db10e5f92f10319c1913e6e9c5`. The
complete unit-test file and the relevant `mla_preprocess_prefill`,
`_get_num_prefill_kv_tokens`, `exec_kv_prefill`, `rope_single`, and
`_forward_prefill` methods are identical to the runtime-tested versions.
A complete E2E rerun of the newer upstream base has not been performed;
other context-handling code changed upstream. This PR remains draft
pending CI/review.

Not covered by the real-model matrix: fused MLA prolog
(`enable_mlapo=true`), prefill graph, MTP, prefix caching, async
scheduling, quantized MLA, other PCP/DCP topologies, GQA E2E, or
performance.

added.subject: [BugFix][xlite] Correct `NZ` flag with `is_tensor_nz` check for MoE gate weights (#17627)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes the `NZ` flags passed to the `xlite` backend for the MoE
gate weights under different NZ modes. Previously, the NZ flag for MoE
gate weights is set to `False` universally, which is incorrect when the
NZ mode is set to 2. This is corrected by checking the tensor format at
runtime instead of hardcoding it.

Additionally, the two flags `mla_wuv_weight_nz` and `mla_wukt_weight_nz`
were added. When `weight_nz_mode` is set to `2`, `WUK_T` has NZ format
for MLA but not DSA, and `WUV` has ND format, instead. (NOTE: this would
require `xlite` update after commit
[f5422970](https://atomgit.com/openeuler/GVirt/commit/f542297065aca1714c5df9e83d11b6e6634d9b5c?ref=master).

Additionally, new logging is added to record the tensor shape, dtype,
and format passed to the `xlite` backend, along with other relevant
configurations.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No, bugfix only.

### How was this patch tested?

`MiniMax-M2.7-w8a8-QuaRot` and `GLM-4.7-W8A8-floatmtp` were tested with
`xlite` full mode + NZ mode set to 0/1/2, and under all 6 scenarios, the
vllm servers returned meaningful answers to single requests.

`DeepSeek-V3.1-w8a8-mtp-QuaRot` and `GLM-5.2-w8a8` were also tested with
the xlite patch
[f5422970](https://atomgit.com/openeuler/GVirt/commit/f542297065aca1714c5df9e83d11b6e6634d9b5c?ref=master)
and the model returned sensible answers, as well.

added.author: Levi
added.subject: [Performance][MoE] Use bf16 router GEMM with fp32 accumulation for bf16-origin weights (#17068)
added.body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

`AscendGateLinear` (PR #9617) forces fp32 weights and fp32 computation
for the MoE router gate, because the previous `bf16×bf16→bf16` path
(bf16 accumulation, no fp32 output) caused expert-selection errors in
agent workloads on NPU.

However, the fp32 path (`aclnnMatmulV2`) is ~6x slower than necessary
for bf16-origin weights — the common case for models like Kimi K3, whose
gate weights are stored as bf16 in safetensors.

This PR makes the bf16 GEMM the default for bf16 router weights, rebuilt
on the same tier architecture as upstream vllm `GateLinear`:

```python
# Tier 4: bf16 weight + bf16 input + fp32 out_dtype + no bias
torch.mm(x, self.weight.t(), out_dtype=torch.float32)
```

which dispatches to `aclnnMm MatMulV3` — bf16 multiplication with **fp32
accumulation**. For bf16-origin operands this is numerically equivalent
to the fp32 path (each `bf16×bf16` product fits exactly in the fp32
accumulator; the only difference is K-dim summation order, ~1e-5).

Two changes make this work end-to-end:

1. **`AscendGateLinear` follows upstream tier-4/tier-5 semantics.** Gate
weights follow the model dtype (no fp32 upcast), so a bf16-origin
checkpoint loads into bf16 params — `self.weight.dtype` is the
checkpoint dtype. The fast-path eligibility is checked at forward time,
mirroring upstream's cuBLAS `out_dtype` epilogue tier.
`force_fp32_compute` is honored exactly like upstream: with no NPU
specialized kernel, it stores the weight in fp32 so the fallback tier
computes in fp32.

2. **`AscendMoERunner` stops forcing fp32 precast on ctor gates.** The
forced `precast_fp32_weight` materialized `weight_fp32` for every
internal-router gate, which made `_compute_router_logits` always bypass
the gate's own forward — so a gate-side fast path could never actually
run for internal-router models (GLM5Next, MiniMax-M3, upstream
DeepSeek-V2 family). fp32 is now a model-level opt-in: DSV4 sets
`precast_fp32_weight` itself and keeps the direct
`F.linear(hidden_states_fp32, gate.weight_fp32)` path; everyone else
routes through `gate(hidden_states)`.

### Key design decisions

- **Weights follow the model dtype** (upstream semantics): no fp32 param
upcast, no `weight_loader` dtype recording, no bf16 weight cache —
`self.weight.dtype` *is* the checkpoint dtype. In-place RL weight
updates are reflected naturally.
- **Eligibility checked at forward time** (mirrors upstream tier 4):
bf16 weight + bf16 input + fp32 `out_dtype` + no bias (`torch.mm` has no
bias term). Any miss falls to tier 5.
- **Tier-5 fallback matches upstream**: cast `x` to the weight dtype,
compute via `ReplicatedLinear.forward`, cast the output to `out_dtype`.
- **`out_dtype=None` defaults to fp32 on NPU** (upstream leaves None and
computes natively): this keeps the historical Ascend fp32-logits
contract for the downstream topk kernels, lets bf16-weight models with
the `out_dtype=None` wiring (upstream DeepSeek-V2 family / GLM5Next)
take tier 4 directly, and resolves the fp32-weight + bf16-input
dtype-mismatch edge.
- **Forced fp32 stays opt-in**: `params_dtype=torch.float32` (e.g.
MiniMax-M3) or `force_fp32_compute` → fp32 weights → tier-5 fp32
compute; DSV4 keeps its `precast_fp32_weight` path routed by the MoE
runner; the 310P runner still forces precast (a forward-time Cast cannot
be captured by ACLGraph on 310P).
- **ACLGraph-safe by construction**: no path casts a weight per forward
— the #16189 failure mode (`gate.weight.to(torch.float32)` emitting an
aclop Cast inside the captured region) is structurally unreachable. Tier
4 contains zero casts at all.

## Background: why the old path was slow

PR #9617 forced fp32 because the pre-existing path was `bf16×bf16→bf16`
(bf16 accumulation). The fast path uses `bf16×bf16→fp32` (fp32
accumulation via `out_dtype=torch.float32`), which avoids the precision
issue while being ~6x faster:

| Path | Multiply | Accumulate | Output | NPU kernel | Speed |
|------|----------|------------|--------|------------|-------|
| Pre-#9617 (bf16 F.linear) | bf16 | bf16 | bf16 | aclnnMatmulV2 |
baseline (broken) |
| #9617 (fp32 F.linear) | fp32 | fp32 | fp32 | aclnnMatmulV2 | 84.8µs |
| **This PR (bf16 mm + fp32 out)** | **bf16** | **fp32** | **fp32** |
**aclnnMm MatMulV3** | **13.7µs (6.2x)** |

## Path routing per model

| Model | Gate wiring | Path after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi K3 | model-side call, bf16 weights, `out_dtype=fp32` | tier 4
(bf16 mm) |
| DeepSeek-V2 family / GLM5Next | runner internal router, bf16 weights,
`out_dtype=None` | tier 4 via `gate()` (fp32 default) |
| MiniMax-M3 | explicit `params_dtype=torch.float32` | tier 5 (fp32,
model intent preserved) |
| DeepSeek-V4 | `precast_fp32_weight` (own) | runner
`F.linear(weight_fp32)` — unchanged |
| 310P internal-router | 310P runner forced precast | unchanged |

## Precision verification

**Methodology**: the fp32 path (`F.linear` → aclnnMatmulV2) and the bf16
path (`torch.mm(out_dtype=fp32)` → aclnnMm MatMulV3) both run **on NPU**
with the production ops; the float64 reference runs **on CPU**. Shape:
N=896, K=7168 (Kimi K3 router).

### M-sweep vs the float64 reference (16 shapes, M = 1 to 896)

Fixed bf16-origin weight [896, 7168]; 16 M values uniformly spaced over
[1, 896]; relative-error denominator = |y_fp64| clamped at 1e-06
(near-zero logits excluded). In both tables, **ratio = bf16 error / fp32
error** (each measured against the same float64 reference); ratio < 1
means the bf16 path is closer to the reference. Top-16 expert selection
(N=896, k=16, per-row expert-set match) is measured on the same outputs
and reported alongside the absolute-error table.

- mean_rel sits at the ~1e-06 scale; max_rel is dominated by near-zero
logits and saturates.
- **Top-16 expert selection is 100% consistent at every shape in this
sweep**: bf16 vs fp32 matches on **7176/7176** rows across all 16
shapes, and both paths vs the float64 reference are likewise 100%
(7176/7176 each).

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No. Router GEMM outputs are unchanged for every model: bf16-origin
weights get the numerically-equivalent `bf16×bf16→fp32` path, and models
that require fp32 routing keep fp32 compute via their existing opt-in
(`params_dtype` / `precast_fp32_weight`).

## How was this patch tested

- Precision test on NPU (Ascend910): compared fp32 path, bf16 path, and
float64 CPU reference across M=3/24/961 with bf16-origin weights (a
true-fp32-weight control, forced through the bf16 math, degrades to
66.7% top-16 consistency — confirming why the weight-dtype condition
matters)
- M-sweep (16 shapes, M=1..896): absolute / relative errors vs float64
CPU reference — bf16 closer on 16/16 shapes; top-16 expert-set match
100% at every shape (bf16 vs fp32: 7176/7176 rows; both paths vs float64
likewise)
- Layout micro-benchmark (nz_bench.py): ND / FRACTAL_NZ /
pre-transposed-NZ bf16 weights produce bit-identical outputs; ND +
`.t()` selected (pre-transposed NZ ~40% slower)
- Unit tests (new): tier-4 fast path (mocked `torch.mm`, asserts
`out_dtype=fp32` and the weight view); params follow the model dtype
unless `force_fp32_compute`; tier-5 fallback casts the output to
`out_dtype`; `out_dtype=None` defaults to fp32 (tier 4 fires directly,
fp32-weight + bf16-input edge resolved)
- Unit tests (runner): init no longer sets `precast_fp32_weight`; gates
without `weight_fp32` route through `gate()` while DSV4-style gates keep
the `F.linear(weight_fp32)` branch
- CI: pre-commit / DCO / cpu-ut green

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Fix 310P KV cache initialization and input handling for MRV1 and MRV2.

- Select attention kernel block sizes that satisfy the hardware limit
and evenly divide the physical KV cache block size. This fixes startup
failures when a 64-token physical block is paired with a 128-token
kernel block.
- Raise `NotImplementedError` when no compatible kernel block size
exists instead of falling back to an unchecked block size.
- Compare MRV1 cache sizes against the initial input batch block size so
the batch is rebuilt when backend selection changes the cache block
size, preventing incorrect KV cache addressing.
- Clear padded input token IDs after the MRV2 decode copy to prevent
stale or out-of-vocabulary IDs from entering FULL decode graphs.

added.subject: [Feature][Attention] Support GQA PCP and DCP stacking (#18065)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

GQA/MQA previously rejected simultaneous prefill and decode context
parallelism. Enable MRV2 stacking for equal PCP and DCP sizes, retaining
each rank's TP-local heads.

Prefill computes current dense K/V attention for local query fragments
and historical attention on DCP-owned KV shards separately. Current K/V
is gathered across PCP; historical queries are gathered and restored by
token order; historical KV remains sharded. Merge partial outputs and
LSE, select local queries and add the current contribution once. Share
history metadata construction and remove redundant history masks while
preserving decode graph-padding behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. GQA/MQA target and draft models can use PCP+DCP only when
`prefill_context_parallel_size == decode_context_parallel_size`. For
example, Qwen3-30B-A3B supports TP8/PCP2/DCP2. The same-size path does
not gather query heads. The constraint is enforced in platform
validation.

This PR targets `main`.

### How was this patch tested?

- Isolated Ascend container validation of this branch's exact source:
**937 passed, 5 skipped** across 18 attention, platform, graph, PCP and
speculative-metadata unit test files. Runtime: vLLM `releases/v0.30.0`
(`ced6857afa`), torch 2.10.0 / torch-npu 2.10.0.post4.
- Added/strengthened coverage for both PCP query-fragment ranks, all
DCP2/DCP4 ranks, uneven/empty history, causal/noncausal KV ordering,
decode/prefill padding, actual FIA Q/K/V inputs and cache-write error
recovery.
- Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 + EAGLE3, MRV2 TP8/PCP2/DCP2
FULL_DECODE_ONLY: GSM8K test first 500, zero-shot CoT, temperature 0,
seed 1024, max output 4096, concurrency 32: **97.00% (485/500)** with
zero request failures. This model run used the remote feature source
before import-only formatting; the exact PR source was rerun through the
unit matrix above.
- Shared-path smoke: DeepSeek-V3.1-w4a8-mtp-QuaRot + MTP3, the same
PCP/DCP topology and graph mode: GSM8K first 500 **96.20% (481/500)**,
zero request failures.
- Repository `format.sh ci` hooks executed, including secret scan and
shell checks. Workflow lint uses pinned actionlint 1.7.7 and ShellCheck
0.11.0 on Linux with verified identical input hashes because the Windows
integration stalls.

Known validation limits: no performance benchmark or full GSM8K baseline
comparison. Earlier deterministic no-speculation PCP+DCP versus TP
logprobs had maximum difference 0.013416, outside atol=rtol=0.01; the
old and reviewed implementations matched each other exactly in that
comparison. Task accuracy does not resolve that cross-topology numeric
gate.

added.subject: [Feature][Worker] Support the TurboQuant packed KV cache in the V1 runner (#18026)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds the **Model Runner V1** half of the TurboQuant 4-bit packed KV
cache.

The packed SFA main cache (`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc`) was
wired through the V2 spec builder only, and a TurboQuant configuration
was rejected outright unless `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. That leaves
deployments still running the V1 runner unable to use the cache at all.
This builds the same spec on the V1 side:

- `worker/model_runner_v1.py`: recognise the attention impl's
`enable_sparse_sfa_turboquant` flag next to the existing C8 one, and
build the 386-byte fused slot (`kv_lora_rank/2` int4 nope bytes + bf16
rope + fp16 scale) with int8 storage. That is the same shape
`worker/v2/attn_utils.py` produces, so the attention implementation
itself stays shared between the two runners.
- Move the V2-runner requirement out of the shared TurboQuant validation
and into the compressed-cache (DeepSeek V4) path, which is the half that
is V2-only. The packed SFA cache is built by both runners, so it no
longer implies one.

Rebased onto `main` after #17726 merged (`72f6b4760`); the diff below is
this change alone.

**Dual merge:** the `releases/v0.30.0` counterpart is #18048 — same
commit, cherry-picked, identical diff (`releases/v0.30.0` already
carries #17726).

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests, in the same commit:

-
`tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py::test_sparse_layer_packs_the_turboquant_main_cache`
— the V1 spec builder produces a packed spec with
`cache_sparse_sfa_turboquant=True`,
`head_size=get_tq_fused_slot_bytes(512, 64)` and `dtype=torch.int8`,
mirroring the C8 spec test next to it.
- `tests/ut/quantization/methods/kv_cache/turboquant/test_config.py` —
an SFA configuration validates without the V2 runner, while the
parametrised case for the DeepSeek V4 path still asserts the
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` requirement.

Neither of these is an end-to-end run: PR CI has no TurboQuant e2e,
because it needs a CANN with `cann_ops_nn.turbo_quant` and the
`key_quant_mode=3` sparse attention operator. The V2 side carries the
same caveat.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, for SFA models only: `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` is no
longer refused when `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` is unset. DeepSeek V4
TurboQuant keeps requiring the V2 runner, and every other constraint
(BF16, `kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`, A2/A3, SFA sparse
models, no xLite, no C8) applies unchanged on both paths.

added.author: recky-c
added.subject: [Feature][PCP] Support graph execution for sharded decode requests (#17958)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Second layer of the PCP decode request sharding series. Builds on #17456
(already merged); the branch is rebased on top of current `main`. The
speculative-decoding layer will follow as a third PR on top of this one.

This layer lifts the graph-execution restriction from #17456: decode
request sharding now works under PIECEWISE and FULL (FULL_DECODE_ONLY)
graphs instead of falling back to the replicated decode path.

- Dispatch graphs with rank-local request counts while retaining the
matching global input capacity, keeping the global batch available for
cache updates and sampling (`get_global_graph_num_reqs`).
- Align local query offsets, restore indices, dummy capture contexts and
empty-rank metadata with the padded graph layout.
- Keep the DSA global RoPE tables at graph-stable addresses in
persistent buffers for FULL graphs, without changing graph-manager code.
- Derive the rank-local request count in `dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp` from
`num_tokens // uniform_token_count`; upstream vLLM #52162 still passes
the global request count (patch documented in
`vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py`).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, as an extension of #17456: eligible configurations that previously
fell back to replicated decode requests under graph execution now shard
decode requests across PCP ranks. Speculative decoding still keeps the
replicated path until the third layer lands.

added.author: lty
added.subject: [Performance]narrow the KV save fence to requests with released blocks (#17555)
added.body:
## 1. Baseline and conclusion

- Baseline: the current save fence in `AscendStoreConnector`.
`handle_preemptions()` calls `KVPoolWorker.wait_for_previous_save()`,
which blocks the scheduler step until the **entire previous save batch**
has drained — i.e. every in-flight put of every request, whether or not
this step reuses any of those blocks.
- This PR narrows the fence to **exactly the requests whose blocks
become reusable this step** (`finished ∪ preempted`), carried through
the connector metadata as `released_req_ids`. Immediate block release is
kept unchanged.
- Measured on Atlas A2 (910B, CANN 9.1.0), Qwen3-32B W8A8, TP4,
single-engine `kv_both` with the mooncake backend:
- High prefix-hit, high-churn workload (16k input / 1-token output,
89.8% external hit): **+49%~52%** Input Token Throughput over the
whole-batch fence.
- No-hit workload (240 prompts, concurrency 60, ~3.5k input):
**+5.3%~5.4%** over the whole-batch fence, and **parity with
no-pooling** (±0.5%, within run-to-run noise) — the residual pooling
overhead in the no-hit case is eliminated.

## 2. Why the whole-batch fence is expensive

The fence exists to protect block reuse: KV blocks are freed immediately
when a request finishes or is preempted, so the in-flight puts reading
those blocks must complete before the scheduler can hand the blocks to a
new request.

The baseline enforces this by waiting for the **whole** previous save
batch on every step the hook fires. That waits for far more than reuse
requires:

- Requests that are still running keep their blocks — nobody can
overwrite them this step, yet the baseline waits for their puts too.
- On workloads with short outputs and high request turnover, many
requests finish every step, the fence fires effectively every step, and
the engine step gets serialized behind the full drain of in-flight RDMA
puts.
- The cost scales with in-flight put volume per step, which matches the
two measured extremes: a long-prompt no-hit workload (few save
completions per step) loses ~4.7% vs no-pooling, while the high-churn
hit workload gives up about a third of the achievable throughput (fence
29488 vs this patch 44400 avg, −33.6%).

## 3. Design

### 3.1 Carry `released_req_ids` in the connector metadata

- `metadata.py` — `AscendConnectorMetadata` gains `released_req_ids:
set[str]`, initialized from `preempted_req_ids`.
- `pool_scheduler.py` — when building the metadata it is set to
`set(scheduler_output.preempted_req_ids) |
set(scheduler_output.finished_req_ids)`.

### 3.2 Fence only those requests on the worker

- `ascend_store_connector.py` — `handle_preemptions()` now calls
`connector_worker.handle_released_saves(meta.released_req_ids)` instead
of `wait_for_previous_save()`.
- `pool_worker.py` — `handle_released_saves()` forwards to the sending
thread's `wait_for_requests_saved()`; the layerwise path is untouched
(its saves are already synchronized at each step's final layer).
- `kv_transfer.py` —
`KVCacheStoreSendingThread.wait_for_requests_saved()` polls
`stored_requests` (1 ms interval) until none of the given request ids
have a queued save chunk left:

```python
def wait_for_requests_saved(self, req_ids: set[str] | None) -> None:
    if not req_ids:
        return
    pending = set(req_ids)
    while True:
        self.raise_if_failed()
        with self.done_task_lock:
            pending &= self.stored_requests.keys()
            if not pending:
                break
        time.sleep(SAVE_REQUEST_POLL_INTERVAL_S)
```

The common case — no request released this step — costs one empty-set
return.

### 3.3 Why draining once is safe

1. A request queues no new save chunks after it finishes or is
preempted.
2. Its terminal state is flushed into exactly one `SchedulerOutput`, so
it appears in `released_req_ids` exactly once.
3. When the fence observes the request has no queued chunks left, every
put it will ever issue has completed — its blocks are safe to reallocate
from then on. No later fence needs to consider it again.
4. Preempted requests are covered by the same set (`preempted_req_ids`
is part of the union), and re-computation re-queues saves under the
still-alive request id, which a later release will fence again.

## 4. Test environment

- Single Atlas A2 server, 8× Ascend 910B, CANN 9.1.0; two containers
from the same image (host network, shared `/data`) used for
cross-checks.
- Server: Qwen3-32B W8A8 (`--quantization ascend`),
`--tensor-parallel-size 4` on NPU 0-3, `--block-size 128`,
`--max-model-len 40960`, `AscendStoreConnector` with `kv_role=kv_both`,
mooncake backend, `HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE=1`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=1`.
- Store: fresh `mooncake_master` per leg
(`--eviction_high_watermark_ratio 0.9 --eviction_ratio 0.15 --port
50088`) with a 20 GB segment config, so every leg starts from an empty
pool.
- Benchmark: ais_bench; metric is **Input Token Throughput** as reported
by the tool.
- Fairness: within each matrix all legs ran on the same machine state,
same image, fresh master; request success counts and external hit rates
are identical across legs, so the deltas are engine-side only.

## 5. Results

### 5.1 High prefix-hit, high-churn workload

`python3 aisbench_test.py --input_len 16384 --output_len 1 --data_num
160 --concurrency 32 --request_rate 0 --dataset_type prefix_cache
--repeat_rate 90% --prefix_num 16 --prefix_test`

16 distinct 16k prefixes, 90% repeat rate → external (pool) hit 89.80%
on **all** legs; local HBM prefix hit 0%; 160/160 requests succeeded on
all legs.

| Build | Input Token Throughput | Duration | Success |
|---|---|---|---|
| fence baseline (whole batch) | 29488.41 | 88.9 s | 160/160 |
| this patch, run 1| 44880.02 | 58.4 s | 160/160 |
| this patch, run 2 | 43920.74 | 59.7 s | 160/160 |

**+49.0% ~ +52.2% vs the fence baseline.** The two patched runs differ
by 2.2%, i.e. single-run noise on this ~60 s workload is ±1-2%; both
runs sit far above the baseline.

### 5.2 No-hit workload vs fence baseline and vs no-pooling

gsm8k 0-shot prompts (mean input ≈ 3500 tokens, no cross-request prefix
sharing → external hit ≈ 0), 240 prompts, concurrency 60.

| Build | Input Token Throughput | TTFT (mean) | ITL (mean) | vs fence |
vs no-pool |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fence baseline (whole batch) | 2157.02 | 7.34 s | 59.9 ms | — | −4.7%
|
| this patch, run 1 | 2273.35 | 6.14 s | 57.4 ms | +5.4% | +0.5% |
| this patch, run 2 | 2271.33 | — | — | +5.3% | +0.4% |
| no-pooling, run 1 | 2262.41 | 6.15 s | 57.7 ms | +4.9% | — |
| no-pooling, run 2 | 2268.15 | — | — | +5.2% | — |

The two patched runs differ by 0.09%; the two no-pooling runs differ by
0.25%. **The patched pool matches no-pooling within ±0.5% (noise), while
the fence baseline gives up ~4.7%.** TTFT and ITL of the patched pool
are identical to no-pooling (6.14 s / 57.4 ms vs 6.15 s / 57.7 ms); the
baseline's TTFT inflation (+1.2 s) is gone.

## 6. Accuracy validation: aisbench GSM8K, 64-way concurrency, pooled vs
no-pool parity (single-node P/D, DeepSeek-V4-Flash)

**Result: with the KV pool demonstrably participating in every request,
pooled accuracy matches no-pooling within sampling noise (max Δ 0.67 pp
= 2/300 flips at temperature 0.6).** Six aisbench GSM8K accuracy runs at
concurrency 64 / request rate 4: cold and warm passes on the P/D + pool
stack, two passes with pool hits on every request, and two no-pooling
single-engine baselines. Across all runs: 0 failed requests, 0
preemptions, 0 errors / 0 tracebacks on every engine.

### 7.1 Results

| # | Stack | Dataset | Accuracy | Pool participation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | P/D + pool, 1st pass (cold) | GSM8K test, 1319 | 85.75 | none
(below granularity) |
| 2 | P/D + pool, 2nd pass (warm) | GSM8K test, 1319 | 86.50 | none; P
local HBM prefix hit 56–68%, P→D transfer on all requests (+1320) |
| 3 | no-pool single engine | GSM8K test, 1319 | 86.05 | — |
| 4 | P/D + pool, 1st pass | long-prefix, 300 | **90.33** | **300/300
requests pool-hit**, each loads 4096 tokens from the pool |
| 5 | P/D + pool, 2nd pass (fully warm) | long-prefix, 300 | **89.67** |
301/301 pool-hit |
| 6 | no-pool single engine | long-prefix, 300 | **90.33** | — |

added.subject: [CI] Add maintenance window to block /nightly and /weekly PR triggers (#17819)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Nightly/weekly PR comment triggers can be paused during a maintenance
window
to protect third-party scheduled tests. A single repository variable
`NIGHTLY_COMMAND_BLOCK_WINDOW` controls the gate, taking an optional
switch
followed by an `HH:MM-HH:MM` range in Beijing time (UTC+8,
cross-midnight
supported, e.g. `true 22:00-08:00`):

- `true 22:00-08:00` -> enabled, block inside the window.
- `22:00-08:00` -> same as above (switch omitted, backward compatible).
- `false 22:00-08:00` -> explicitly disabled.
- unset/invalid -> disabled with a warning (fail-open).

Switch aliases are true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off (case-insensitive);
space
or comma separators are accepted. The `authorize` job exports a
`blocked`
output, the resolve step is guarded, and every dispatch job plus
`post-links`
checks it. Scheduled runs and other commands (/e2e, /rerun, ...) are
unaffected.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

added.subject: [BugFix][CI] Skip empty A3 and A5 nightly matrices (#18096)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The nightly workflows can fail while their selected test jobs succeed.
The matrix resolver emits `[]` when a test configuration section is
absent, and GitHub Actions rejects an empty `test_config` matrix before
creating a job.

- In A3, guard `single-node-tests` and `multi-card-tests` when
`a3.single_node.test_config` or `a3.multi_card.test_config` is absent.
Examples of the workflow-level matrix error: [run
36678576723](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/36678576723)
and [run
37806214964](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/37806214964).
- In A5, guard `multi-node-tests` and `single-node-tests`. The current
A5 config has no `a5.multi_node.test_config`, so the unguarded
multi-node matrix has the same failure mode.
- Require `setup-vars` to succeed before consuming its outputs, so a
missing output from a failed setup job cannot reach `fromJson`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. A3 and A5 nightly runs with absent test configuration sections skip
those jobs instead of failing at matrix expansion. Model inference
behavior is unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Confirmed the A3 failures linked above report `Matrix vector
'test_config' does not contain any values` for absent matrix sections.
- Applied the same A3 guard in the test repository:
[nv-action/vllm-benchmarks run
37893486430](https://github.com/nv-action/vllm-benchmarks/actions/runs/37893486430)
completed successfully, including a selected single-node test; no job
failed.
- Verified that the A5 config lacks `a5.multi_node.test_config` and that
the resolver emits `[]` for missing sections.
- `git diff --check` and the GitHub Actions workflow lint hook passed
for both changes. The local `codespell` and Gitleaks hooks could not
start for the A5 commit on Windows, so they were skipped with approval;
the remaining hooks passed.

No unit test was added because the failure occurs in GitHub Actions
matrix evaluation before a runner starts. The A3 test-repository run
exercises the guard; A5 still requires a workflow run for end-to-end
validation.

added.author: Ye Chenglin
added.subject: [BugFix][Attention] Respect per-layer KV cache dtype (#18003)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, MiniMax-M3 on Ascend A5 uses the mixed-KV
policy introduced in #17389: GQA layers are added to
`kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` and retain BF16 KV, while sparse layers use
FP8. Upstream `Attention` resolves the skip-layer override and passes
the effective per-layer dtype to the backend.

`AscendAttentionBackendImpl` currently ignores that argument and reads
the global cache dtype again. As a result, a BF16 GQA layer is treated
as FP8 and startup fails with:

```text
ValueError: The current GQA-related models adopt static quantization.
KV quantization is configured via "--kv-cache-dtype" upon service startup
```

Use the constructor's `kv_cache_dtype` argument when resolving the
backend dtype. Keep the existing static-quantization validation. This
completes the backend handling needed by the mixed-KV policy; the
global-dtype read already existed before #17389.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Layers with a KV dtype override now use their effective per-layer dtype.
No CLI or configuration change is introduced. Quantized layers without
the required static quantized weights still raise an error.

### How was this patch tested?

- The new layer-override regression test fails with the original GQA
ValueError before the fix.
- After applying this fix to the installed backend, `python -m pytest -q
tests/ut/attention/test_attention_v1.py` passes: **40 passed**. The
added tests cover global FP8 with layer auto/BF16, with and without the
recipe C8 flag, and preserve rejection of a genuinely quantized layer
lacking quantized weights.
- `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `codespell`, forbidden-import and
boolean-context-manager hooks, and `git diff --check` pass for the
changed files.
- Full `format.sh ci` did not complete because pre-commit's Go
environment download for actionlint failed with `zipfile.BadZipFile`;
this is not reported as a full CI pass.
- On two Ascend 950DT hosts (vLLM `0.30.0+empty`, vllm-ascend
`0.19.1rc2.dev2602+geee24e2e6.d20261007`, PyTorch `2.10.0`, torch-npu
`2.10.0.post7`), Prefill and Decode startup with DP2/TP4, MXFP8 model
weights, FP8 KV and EAGLE3 BF16 KV both pass the original GQA
initialization failure after this fix.
- **End-to-end PD validation completed with this fix plus the
independent block-alignment fix in #18014.** After the HCCL environment
repair, #18014 resolves the separate M3 Indexer metadata assertion
during graph capture. Both D ranks complete 81 FULL graphs; all four P/D
APIs are healthy. Fifteen PD requests pass, including four-way
concurrency, repeated 7742-token inputs and 299-token outputs. Both D
ranks record external KV transfer; zero preemptions or request errors.
This is startup/inference smoke coverage, not a performance or
model-accuracy benchmark.

The GQA patch is unchanged. The graph/block-alignment change is kept
exclusively in #18014; deploy both fixes for the reproduced mixed-KV
setup.

### CI refresh (2026-10-09)

Rebased onto `main@8fadbe0` to refresh the PR workflow after #17997
renamed the custom operator to `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h_vllm`. The
previous CI attempt successfully rebased the tested source onto
`a50eb57`, which contains #17997, but its previously loaded workflow
still checked the old `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` name. This explains
the stale-name registration failure; it is not evidence that the new
operator is missing.

The fix and regression-test patch are unchanged (identical stable patch
ID); author/committer/DCO are preserved. Ruff check/format and `git diff
--check` pass after rebase. Previously documented unit/hardware results
remain historical; the fresh CI run validates this rebased head.

added.author: Jinzhu Jia
added.subject: [BugFix][Worker] Preserve PIECEWISE dummy query widths with DP and MTP (#18038)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

With MRV2, DP and MTP enabled, an idle rank can fail in the draft model
with `AssertionError: reusing a DP sync taken over a different batch`.
PIECEWISE pads the dummy model inputs while keeping the request count
unchanged. Redistributing padded tokens into dummy queries changes the
uniform query width after the target model has already synchronized it
across DP ranks.

Preserve the original dummy query token count while padding the
persistent model-input views. Match dummy attention metadata and slot
mappings to those padded inputs, and restore the scoped token count even
if execution raises.

Apply this to pure PIECEWISE dummy runs without PCP or hybrid model
state, including runs with nonzero `context_len`. Profiling remains
eager with its existing layout, and Ascend already disables
microbatching, so neither needs an extra eligibility guard.

Known limitation: a context-bearing dummy run that also pads token
inputs can fail in upstream `set_dummy_context()`, which copies
logical-token positions into the padded position view.

The existing graph dispatch and DP collective are preserved.
Real-request execution gains no additional synchronization or
allocations.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

N/A

### How was this patch tested?

#### GPQA Diamond accuracy

rounds per configuration without restarting the service. MRV2, DSpark5,
target/draft `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, Engram CPU offload and shared memory
enabled, `temperature=0`, and `enable_thinking=False`.

| Configuration | Ascend commit | Accuracy (3 rounds) | Median accuracy
| Median DSpark acceptance |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline: TP1/PCP1/DP8 | `4cbe4962c` | 73%, 76%, 74% | 74% | 54.68% |
| PCP: TP1/PCP8/DP1 | `b2cfa15ce` | 76%, 76%, 76% | 76% | 60.73% |

All 300 requests per configuration succeeded. Truncated/unparseable
answers remain in the 100-question denominator. DSpark acceptance is
accepted/proposed draft tokens from formal-stage metric deltas.

#### Prefill performance with Engram enabled

8 Ascend A5 NPUs, DSACP TP2/PCP1/DP4 vs PCP TP1/PCP2/DP4, EP8. MRV2,
DSpark5, target/draft `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, Engram CPU offload and shared
memory. Measured on Ascend `e6433e4c0` before rebase, with vLLM
`ced6857a`.

One round, 16 requests per case, 1 output token. Prefill time is the
server-side mean; input throughput is measured over the request wall

added.author: freyfwt
added.subject: [Feature][Model] Support EPLB for Kimi K3 and its MTP draft model (#17835)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Upstream Kimi K3 declares `MixtureOfExperts` but does not initialize the
runtime metadata required by `is_mixture_of_experts()`, so EPLB
registration skips the model. This PR implements that contract for the
Ascend language model and MoE MTP draft, and exposes the language model
through the multimodal wrapper.

- Main and MTP adapters share MoE bookkeeping. EPLB layer counts match
the actual MoE layers in each PP stage; stages without local routed
experts are skipped.
- `AscendKimiMoE` passes EPLB settings to `FusedMoEFactory` and reads
its validated expert counts, including effective EP configuration and
divisibility checks. Redundant experts are zero when EPLB is disabled.
- A shared streaming helper loads the complete initial physical-expert
layout. This includes MRV2 layouts with replicas interspersed across EP
ranks: loading only physical IDs beyond the logical expert count would
leave earlier slots incorrectly initialized. The helper streams remapped
physical expert names through upstream and loads the remaining replica
slots directly with existing parameter loaders. Packed weights, scales,
upstream loaded-parameter tracking, MTP name rewriting and checkpoint
validation are covered.
- Physical metadata updates preserve the fixed local-slot capacity of
allocated expert tensors.

The dense DSpark draft has no routed experts and is skipped by EPLB
registration.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Kimi K3 and its MoE MTP draft can register with EPLB on Ascend,
with correct initial replica loading and PP-local state sizing. When
EPLB is disabled, weights stream directly to upstream.

### How was this patch tested?

- Focused CPU tests with dependency stubs: **265 passed** across
`tests/ut/models/test_kimi_k3_eplb.py`,
`tests/ut/models/test_kimi_k3_adapter.py`,
`tests/ut/models/test_kimi_k3_pp_sp.py`, and
`tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_mtp_eplb.py`. Worker registration and
unavailable `fla_npu` imports were stubbed; the kernel stubs raise if
executed. These results validate Python/control flow, not NPU execution.
- Regression comparison against the previous PR head: **25 failed, 80
passed** with the updated EPLB tests and unchanged production code. The
failures reproduce MRV2 loading and PP-local metadata/state bugs; all
pass after the fix. A test-only alias bridges the renamed helper for
this comparison.
- Independent review: 795 layout/order combinations and 72 combinations
using the pinned upstream main/MTP loader methods passed CPU/AST checks,
including the 256 logical + 8 redundant expert layout with EP=8.
- `bash format.sh ci`: passed all hooks.
- Full `tools/mypy.sh 1` for Python **3.10, 3.11 and 3.12**: passed for
`vllm_ascend`, `examples` and `tests`, against the verified vLLM commit
below. Static validation used NumPy 1.26.4, installed Triton source for
module discovery, and a temporary native-extension discovery stub.
- Real NPU validation remains unverified because the configured
validation hosts could not be reached/authenticated. No NPU kernel or
end-to-end accuracy result is claimed.

### What this PR does / why we need it?
This PR implements TurboQuant (TQ) 4-bit KV cache packing and shared read-only transforms optimized for DeepSeek-V4 (DSV4) DSpark.

- Adds a fused Triton kernel `turboquant_finalize` to correct TQ scale and pack cache rows in a single launch, preventing recompilation for arbitrary row counts.

added.author: XuChi
added.subject: [BugFix][Model] Point users at the recipe fix when oproj capacity is exceeded (#18126)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Improves the `ValueError` raised in `dsa_v1.py::_forward_o_proj` when
the fine-grained oproj TP static exchange capacity cannot cover the
local token count. The old message only echoed two numbers:

```
ValueError: oproj static exchange capacity must cover local tokens, got 16 and 240.
```

Real user case: DeepSeek-V4-Flash + PD disaggregation (decode dp16×tp1)
with `--max-num-batched-tokens 240 --max-num-seqs 4`, speculative
decoding (dql=4), and `finegrained_tp_config
{"oproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8}` crashed at startup with the message
above. The capacity is `max(largest capture bucket,
min(max_num_batched_tokens, max_num_seqs * decode_query_len))` = 16
while the profiling/warmup dummy batch equals `max_num_batched_tokens` =
240, so the raise fired — but users could not tell (a) that this is a
fine-grained-TP recipe constraint rather than an engine bug, or (b) how
to fix the config.

The new message states the constraint (`capacity >=
max_num_batched_tokens`) and both fixes — set `--max-num-batched-tokens`
to `max_num_seqs * decode_query_len`, or raise the largest entry of
`cudagraph_capture_sizes` — with the user's `max_num_seqs` inlined.
Rendered at the user's numbers:

```
oproj static exchange capacity (16) must cover local tokens (240). Fine-grained oproj TP requires capacity >= max_num_batched_tokens. Please set --max-num-batched-tokens to max_num_seqs * decode_query_len (currently max_num_seqs=4), or raise the largest cudagraph_capture_sizes entry.
```

Message style follows the repo's existing compound-error precedent
(`profiling_chunk_config` in `ascend_config.py`: fact + numbers +
"Please set X, or Y"; the second fix names the actual config key,
matching the knob-naming style of the `potential_max_tokens` warning in
`utils.py`). `scheduler_config` is read from `self.vllm_config` — the
same object the capacity computation three lines above already uses —
inside the failure branch only, so there is zero hot-path cost.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Only the error message text, which becomes actionable. No behavior
change.

### How was this patch tested?

- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` pass locally, and the rendered
message was verified by local string simulation (pasted above).
- The existing UT `test_o_proj_capacity_covers_profile_and_decode`
asserted the old message text, so its `pytest.raises` match is updated
to the new core fragment and now also asserts the inlined numbers
(`capacity (N) must cover local tokens (M)`); its `scheduler_config`
mock gains the `max_num_seqs` attribute the raise path now reads. No
vllm/torch environment on this machine, so UT verification relies on CI;
the change is a single error-message edit and needs no NPU run.

Title: [Performance][Quantization] Release dead W8A8 fp32 MoE scales
under MegaMoe

---
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Part 2 of 2 (quantization side). In
`AscendW8A8DynamicFusedMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading`, the
`use_cann_megamoe` branch switches consumers over to
`cann_mega_moe_fused_w*_scale_list` (unbind views), but the dense
`w13/w2_weight_scale_fp32` fp32 blocks allocated earlier stay resident
and are never read on this path — dead memory. The EPLB branch in the
same function already follows the `del + torch.npu.empty_cache()`
pattern; `routed_experts.py` has the same precedent for the weights
themselves.

This PR releases the dead fp32 scale blocks in the MegaMoe branch (gated
to non-EPLB, which is structurally mutually exclusive with the MegaMoe
branch via the existing if/elif). Frees ~0.15–0.4 GiB per card on W8A8
MoE deployments, on top of part 1 (attention side).

Known follow-up (out of scope): the `del` lacks an activation guard for
the MiniMax-M3 `swigluoai_uninterleave` + `enable_fused_mc2=2`
combination, which has no in-tree e2e config today.

### How was this patch tested?

- `tests/ut/quantization/methods/w8a8/test_w8a8_dynamic.py`: new case
asserting the dead attributes are released on the MegaMoe path and

added.author: Wei Yubo
added.subject: [BugFix][Spec Decode] Size DFlash query buffers for ACL graph padding (#17379)
added.body:
Fixes #18121

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix a query-buffer capacity issue in DFlash speculative decoding on the
vLLM Ascend V1 model runner.

`AscendDflashProposer` allocates its persistent query buffers using
`max_query_tokens = max_batch_size * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)`.
However, ACLGraph dispatch may select a padded execution size larger
than this logical limit.

For example, 33 requests with 3 speculative tokens have a logical query
limit of 132. If graph dispatch selects 136 tokens, slicing a
132-element positions buffer with `[:136]` still returns only 132
elements, potentially producing inconsistent model input shapes.
Whether this occurs depends on the configured capture sizes.

This PR introduces:

`max_padded_query_tokens = max(max_query_tokens,
compilation_config.max_cudagraph_capture_size or 0)`

The padded capacity is used for `positions`, `_slot_mapping_buffer`,
and `max_positions` / `arange_dflash`, ensuring that allocation covers
the configured graph execution range.

The logical `max_query_tokens` limit, context buffers, dtypes, and
devices remain unchanged. The change only affects initialization-time
allocation and adds no per-step allocation or synchronization.

`AscendDflash2Proposer` inherits the same allocation and is also
covered.

Adapted from [vLLM PR
#50065](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50065).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Corrects buffer sizing for V1 DFlash/DFlash2 configurations where graph
padding exceeds the logical query limit. No new configuration options
or API changes are introduced.

### How was this patch tested?

Added 12 parameterized regression cases in
`tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash_proposer.py`, covering both DFlash
and DFlash2 with:

- Padded execution larger than the logical query limit.
- Capture-aligned and equal-capacity cases.
- A logical query limit larger than the capture limit.
- Unset (`None`) and zero capture limits.

The tests verify buffer slice shapes, dtypes, devices, and preservation
of logical query and context limits. The existing dummy slot mapping
cleanup test is retained.

After merging main, commit `35815e701` passed CPU CI against both
vLLM `ced6857afa` and `v0.30.0`. Each run reported
**8341 passed, 70 skipped, 17 warnings**. All 12 new regression cases
and the existing cleanup test passed in both runs. Pre-commit also
passed.

- [vLLM main CPU
CI](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/37716116727/job/113114196146)
- [vLLM v0.30.0 CPU
CI](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/37716116727/job/113114196236)

These tests validate allocation and slicing on CPU. NPU graph
capture/replay, inference correctness, and memory/performance
validation remain outstanding. The required selected/full tests
are awaiting maintainer triggering.

added.author: Ye Chenglin
added.subject: [BugFix][Attention] Use a 64-token kernel minimum for M3 FP8 KV (#18125)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

MiniMax M3 with FP8 KV on hardware supporting FP8 attention retains BF16
KV in its GQA layers. The Ascend dense attention backend currently
advertises only a 128-token kernel block. Upstream heterogeneous-KV
alignment therefore expands the primary FP8 block to 256 tokens, which
is incompatible with the M3 indexer's 128-token block and causes
graph-capture initialization to fail.

For M3 FP8/FP8_E4M3 configurations with skip-quantization layers,
advertise dense kernel blocks `[64, 128]`. The existing upstream
alignment can then select 128 as the final cache block while keeping 128
available as the common kernel size with M3 sparse/indexer backends.
Gate this on `HardwareCapability.FP8_ATTENTION`; other models, non-FP8
configurations, configurations without skip layers, and calls outside an
engine context keep `[128]`.

Keep the initial cache block at 128. Setting `cache_config.block_size =
64` early in `utils.refresh_block_size` is insufficient on its own, and
doing so together with the backend change leaves the runner's
pre-model-load block table at 64 after alignment updates the cache
configuration to 128. In the reproduced single-group setup the existing
input-batch reinitialization check does not detect that transition. This
patch avoids that transition and requires no runner change.

This is an alternative to #18014 that retains upstream alignment. It
does not contain #18014's platform override or #18003's per-layer dtype
fix. The reproduced mixed-KV setup still needs #18003; validate/deploy
this PR with that fix and without #18014.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The affected M3 mixed-KV configuration can initialize and run with the
supported 128-token cache/kernel block. No new CLI flag or environment
variable is introduced. The value 64 is a backend minimum used by
alignment, not the final block size of every layer. This PR does not
claim a measured KV-memory saving.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added 16 configuration regression cases covering both M3
architectures, both FP8 strings, explicit/default block settings,
repeated upstream alignment, other models/dtypes/hardware, absent engine
context, absent skip layers, and preservation of a separate draft
model's shared cache configuration.
- Ran the new cases and the existing attention tests against the patched
serving-image modules: **56 passed**. Restoring the original `[128]`
backend declaration in an isolated process causes all eight mixed-KV
alignment cases to fail with `256 != 128`. These are configuration
tests, not full model loading.
- On Ascend 950DT, ran eight small BF16 paged-GQA operator checks with
64/128-token pages, noncontiguous block tables, KV lengths
65/129/257/1025 and query lengths 1/4/16. All pass against an FP32
reference (`atol=0.01`, `rtol=0.02`); maximum observed absolute error
was 0.002543.
- Single-host, eight-device **DP2/TP4** serving with MiniMax-M3 MXFP8
weights, FP8 KV, EAGLE3 BF16 KV/spec3, max model length 133000, max
sequences 256 and FULL_DECODE_ONLY/max graph capture 1024. #18003 was
retained and #18014 removed. Both DP ranks complete **81 FULL graphs**
and both APIs become healthy. **14/14** inference requests pass,
including concurrent requests, four 7741-token inputs with prefix reuse,
and four exact 1-to-100 outputs of 299 tokens.
- Runtime cache inspection confirms the runner's initial block, actual
block-table dimensions, cache specs and selected common kernel block are
all 128. GQA, sparse, indexer and draft caches retain their actual
per-layer byte strides. Temporary cache-audit instrumentation was
removed from installed source after validation; it is not included in
this PR.
- Serving validation used vLLM `0.30.0+empty`, vllm-ascend
`0.19.1rc2.dev2602+geee24e2e6.d20261007`, PyTorch `2.10.0` and torch-npu
`2.10.0.post7`, with the changed functions applied to that image. The
production function ASTs were checked against this PR. This is not a
full integration run of the current main checkout, a performance
benchmark, a full accuracy evaluation or a maximum-context test.
Two-host PD was not rerun because the second host was unavailable; the
single-host test omits KV-transfer configuration.
- Changed-file Ruff check/format, codespell, typos, forbidden-import
checks, boolean-context checks and `git diff --check` pass. Full local
`format.sh ci` stalled while installing actionlint's Go environment and
was stopped after 90 seconds; a full local lint/CI pass is not claimed.

Author, committer and DCO: `yingyingzizi <1084697284@qq.com>`.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

After upgrading or downgrading CANN, previously compiled artifacts and
cached build results may be incompatible with the updated environment.
Reinstalling vLLM Ascend without cleaning them may reuse stale artifacts
and lead to build or runtime compatibility issues.

- Rebuilding custom kernels and reinstalling vLLM Ascend from source.

before rebuilding.

behavior, APIs, or build logic.

added.author: Ronald
added.subject: [BugFix][Model] Apply DeepSeek-V4 attention sinks through the weight loader (#16958)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek-V4 Attention Sink loading used direct `copy_` calls, bypassing
the parameter's current `weight_loader`. During live/layerwise reload,
those writes land on meta parameters instead of entering the reload
cache, leaving the original Sink values unchanged.

Route the Target, MTP and DSpark Sink branches through
`param.weight_loader`, with `default_weight_loader` as the fallback.
Keep TP slicing in `load_weights`, preserve full-Sink loading under DSA
CP, and keep DSpark's existing `[head_start:head_end]` slice. No shared
abstraction or upstream reload framework changes are introduced.

The final diff contains only the three Sink loading files and
`tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_weight_loader_reload.py`. Runtime
RMSNorm ownership, attention quantization scales, sleep/wake fixes and
E2E enablement have been removed. DeepSeek-V4 remains skipped in both
NPU IPC and HCCL E2E lanes using the baseline `skip_reason` logic.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Live/layerwise weight updates now apply new Attention Sink values.
Ordinary checkpoint loading and TP/DSA CP partitioning remain unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Expanded the Sink UT to **102 cases**:

| Coverage | Target | MTP | DSpark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP=1/2/4/8, every rank, custom loader | 15 | 15 | 15 |
| TP=1/2/4/8, every rank, default loader | 15 | 15 | 15 |
| DSA CP, TP=2/rank=1, custom/default loader | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Real layerwise reload, two successive updates, TP and DSA CP | 2 | 2 |
2 |

Custom-loader tests assert exactly one call, the actual destination
Parameter, exact tensor values/shape, and unchanged parameter contents
when the recording loader does not copy. Checkpoint names traverse the
production mappings, including MTP's `mtp_block` and DSpark's real
`_remap_dspark_name` (`mtp.1.attn.attn_sink` ->
`model.layers.4.self_attn.attn_sink` with three target layers).

Local Windows CPU validation (PyTorch 2.7.1+cpu): **102 passed**. This
was a **source-isolated run**, not a successful canonical repository
pytest run: it compiled the complete production `load_weights` methods
and real name-mapping methods directly from the changed files, isolated
unrelated serving/NPU imports, and ran this test file through pytest.
The reload implementation itself was imported unmodified from upstream
vLLM at `ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607` (the merged base's
verified dependency), including its metadata/meta/materialization
helpers; no replacement reload wrapper was written. All six lifecycle
cases verify startup A -> reload B -> reload C and unchanged original
storage addresses.

Regression sensitivity was verified by temporarily replacing the three
Sink loader calls with direct copies: **54 failed, 48 passed**,
including failures in all six lifecycle cases. The production files were
restored byte for byte; rerunning the fixed version gave **102 passed**.

Canonical `python -m pytest
tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_weight_loader_reload.py -q` is blocked
at conftest import by missing `uvloop` on Windows. A direct collection
attempt with `--confcutdir=tests/ut/models` is also blocked by the
installed Transformers dependency (`PreTrainedConfig` import). Canonical
Linux/NPU CI remains required; no H20 or E2E run was performed.

Passed locally: Ruff check/format on all four files, Python compilation,
`git diff --check`, forbidden-import, boolean-context-manager,
long-function, package-init and symbolic-meta checks. The full
`format.sh ci` run passed Ruff 0.14.0 check/format, codespell, typos,
clang-format, Markdown lint, actionlint, PNG lint, filename checks,
package-init, forbidden imports and boolean-context-manager checks. The
full gate did not pass on Windows: Gitleaks/logger hooks could not find
`/bin/bash`, ShellCheck is not installed, and the
long-function/symbolic-meta hooks could not resolve `python3`. The
latter Python checks passed when invoked directly with `python`; the
logger check also passed when invoked directly with Git Bash. These
environment failures are not reported as a green full gate.

Refs #16355, #16322.

added.author: drslark
added.subject: [BugFix] Define draft token mapping for full-vocabulary DSpark models (#18182)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Define `draft_id_to_target_id = None` on the Ascend DeepSeek V4 and
DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark model classes. Their draft token IDs already match
target token IDs, so they need no remapping. This exposes the attribute
read by the DSpark speculator.

The latest models were checked, including the newly added GLM5 DSpark.
Qwen3 initializes its mapping in the upstream constructor, and GLM5
initializes its own mapping depending on vocabulary size. Preserve both
paths: adding a class-level default to Qwen3 could interfere with
registration of GLM5's reduced-vocabulary mapping parameter.

Corresponding vLLM file:
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py`
(`DSparkSpeculator.load_draft_model`).

The upstream DSpark speculator reads the mapping attribute directly:

```python
# vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py::DSparkSpeculator
def load_draft_model(
    self,
    target_model: torch.nn.Module,
    target_attn_layer_names: set[str],
) -> torch.nn.Module:
    model = load_dspark_model(target_model, self.vllm_config)
    # Reduced draft vocab: probabilistic rejection sampling indexes draft
    # logits by target id, so precompute the draft->target column map and a
    # scratch buffer to scatter logits into target vocab before sampling.
    if self.draft_logits is not None and model.draft_id_to_target_id is not None:
        ...
```

Full-vocabulary draft models must expose `draft_id_to_target_id = None`
so this check can skip vocabulary remapping without raising an
`AttributeError`.

Kimi K3 already inherits `draft_id_to_target_id = None` from its
upstream `K3DSparkForCausalLM` class, so no change is needed for Kimi
K3.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Avoid a missing mapping attribute for full-vocabulary DSpark models. No
new flags or configuration changes.

### How was this patch tested?

1. Added `tests/ut/models/test_dspark_vocab_mapping.py`, parameterized
over DeepSeek V4 and V4.1. It checks `hasattr(draft,
"draft_id_to_target_id")` on real draft model instances without
allocating model weights. The test comment explains that vLLM's
`DSparkSpeculator.load_draft_model` directly reads this attribute. The
test only checks attribute presence, not its value.
2. Ran `python -m pytest -q
tests/ut/models/test_dspark_vocab_mapping.py` against both branch source
trees: **2 passed** for each. Tests ran in the A3 container with vLLM
commit `ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607`; no model weights or
NPU inference were needed.
3. Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed. The full repository
test/hook suite and model inference were not run to completion.

added.subject: [Feature][P/D] Support Mooncake V2 KV receive failure handling (#18146)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Support request-level KV receive failure reporting in
`MooncakeConnectorV2` through vLLM's `KVConnectorTransferResults`,
including hybrid caches with multiple KV groups. Drain receive
completion and failure together, attribute transfer errors to the
affected requests, and retain producer release notifications after
worker completion is aggregated. Log failed request IDs and the
configured failure policy on D.

Preserve externally supplied request IDs in the PD proxy, with
`X-Request-Id` taking precedence over the JSON body. Update existing
connector tests for the new completion results.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Multi-group KV transfer failures follow `kv_load_failure_policy`
instead of being ignored. When this option is omitted, vLLM defaults to
`fail`, so failed KV transfers are handled as request failures without
any additional configuration. Clients can supply a request ID through
the proxy and correlate it with failure logs.

### How was this patch tested?

Ascend A5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `MooncakeConnectorV2`, P/D DP4 TP1,
six KV groups, and `kv_load_failure_policy=fail`. Injected receive
failures based on externally supplied request IDs, using both header and
body IDs; the randomized phase used concurrency 4.

| Requests | HTTP 200 | HTTP 500 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deterministic and recovery checks | 8 | 3 |
| Randomized injection | 53 | 47 |
| Total | 61 | 50 |

All 111 requests matched the expected outcome. All 50 failed requests
reached `FINISHED_ERROR`; P-side release and D-side cleanup were
verified. Running/waiting requests and KV-cache usage returned to zero
on all P/D ranks. Temporary fault-injection code is excluded from this
PR.

These runs cover simulated receive failures, not actual network faults
or same-request cross-TP failure aggregation.

added.author: muziyuhui666
added.subject: [BugFix][MoE] Handle missing MegaMoE activation kwargs (#18137)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR prevents the CANN MegaMoE path from raising a `TypeError` when
the routed layer's `mega_moe_activation_kwargs` is `None`.

`FusedMC2CommImpl._apply_cann_mega_moe()` currently expands the layer
attribute directly:

```python
**layer.mega_moe_activation_kwargs
```

However, this attribute may be `None` when the per-layer MegaMoE
activation metadata is unavailable. Expanding it as keyword arguments
results in the following exception:

```text
TypeError: argument after ** must be a mapping, not NoneType
```

This change resolves the MegaMoE activation arguments in the following
order:

1. Use the activation arguments bound to the current routed layer.
2. Fall back to the activation arguments resolved by the shared
communicator.
3. Use an empty mapping if neither source provides activation arguments.

The layer-specific arguments remain preferred. This preserves the
correct activation parameters for models and layers that provide them,
while preventing MegaMoE inference from crashing when the layer metadata
is missing.

The existing MegaMoE unit test is updated to cover the case where
`layer.mega_moe_activation_kwargs` is `None` and to verify that the
communicator's resolved activation arguments are passed to the CANN
MegaMoE operator.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with the implementation
and test update. I reviewed the resulting diff and take responsibility
for the submitted change.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

NO

### How was this patch tested?

added.author: muziyuhui666
added.subject: [BugFix][MoE] Fix E8M0 scale dtype for CANN MegaMoE (#18157)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes the E8M0 weight scale dtype passed to CANN MegaMoE by the
W8A8-MXFP8 and W4A4-MXFP4 fused MoE implementations.

The E8M0 weight scales are stored in checkpoints as `uint8` tensors.
When preparing the per-expert scale lists for CANN MegaMoE, the existing
implementation only clones these tensors, leaving their dtype as
`torch.uint8`.

However, `npu_mega_moe` requires `l1_weights_sf` and `l2_weights_sf` to
use the semantic dtype `torch.float8_e8m0fnu`. As a result, models using
these quantization schemes fail during the profiling run with an error
similar to:

`RuntimeError: l1_weights_sf[0] dtype must be float8_e8m0fnu, but got
Byte.`

This PR:

- Reinterprets the cloned W8A8-MXFP8 MegaMoE weight scales as
`torch.float8_e8m0fnu`.
- Reinterprets the cloned W4A4-MXFP4 MegaMoE weight scales as
`torch.float8_e8m0fnu`.
- Applies the fix to both the `w13`/L1 and `w2`/L2 scale lists.
- Preserves the original E8M0 bit patterns by using
`view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu)` instead of performing a numeric dtype
conversion.
- Adds unit tests covering the resulting dtype and bit-pattern
preservation.

The change is limited to the CANN MegaMoE weight preparation paths for
these two quantization schemes.

NO

added.author: ZixuanWang
added.subject: [BugFix][Worker] Zero static KV buffers after cudagraph capture (#17659)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Zero every KV-cache / recurrent-state tensor in `static_forward_context`
right after cudagraph capture (v1 NPU model runner).

**Root cause (pinned down):** on GLM-5.3-Flash the KDA (mamba)
conv/recurrent state caches share backing storage with the SFA fp8 KV
pool — per 4-layer group, the `layers.{4,5,6}` KDA state tensors and the
`layers.7` SFA pool have identical `data_ptr` (verified empirically for
every layer group, on **both** vLLM 0.29 and 0.30, so the co-location is
plugin-side arena behavior, not a vLLM-version artifact). During
cudagraph capture/warmup the dummy forward really executes the KDA write
path over those shared slots: `causal_conv1d` writes conv_state at
slot+0 (0xC000 B) and `recurrent_kda` writes recurrent_state at
slot+0xC000 (0x80000 B) — 573440 B in total, i.e. exactly pool blocks
0–8, byte-for-byte matching the observed post-capture corruption. That
bf16 dummy state contains NaN/±inf; reinterpreted as fp8 e4m3, bytes
0x7F/0xFF are NaN encodings. NaN survives the additive softmax mask (NaN
+ -inf = NaN — unlike finite garbage, which the mask drives to zero
weight), so the first real request reads poisoned pages, the residual
stream is contaminated, logits collapse to NaN, and generation degrades
into emitting 64 consecutive "!" tokens (GSM8K accuracy drops).

**What flipped between 0.29 and 0.30:** both versions alias the KDA
states into the SFA pool (byte-identical addresses — plugin-side arena
behavior, not a vLLM-version artifact) and both dirty the pool during
capture; they differ in how capture *ends*. 0.30 finishes with 73/104
persistent tensors holding 2,332,162 NaNs — activation probes show NaN
in all layers at all 6 captured sizes, so every pass re-poisons the
states. 0.29 finishes clean (0/104): in its last (smallest) capture
passes the main model stops ingesting the dirty bytes, hidden states
collapse to zero, and zero-valued KDA state writes cascade-clean every
pool (reproduced twice, event counts byte-identical). The upstream line
responsible for this difference is **not yet pinned**: a direct verdict
experiment on 0.30 with `ModelConfig.get_head_size()` forced back to the
0.29 value (64) still ends 73/104 dirty, which experimentally excludes
the `is_deepseek_mla()` head-size flip in vllm-project/vllm#53906 as the
trigger (the head_dim metadata field it changes has no functional
consumer in either codebase — verified by exhaustive search). The fork
lies elsewhere in the 0.29→0.30 diff; candidates under investigation are
#53906's mamba-metadata `positions` link and its sparse-indexer/kpool
changes. This open question does not affect the fix: the corruption is
capture-time-only, runtime page allocations are disjoint from the dummy
writes, and zeroing after capture restores the logically-empty start
state on both versions alike.

**Why Ascend A3 (910B) is immune:** fp8 KV cache is assert-disabled on
that platform, so C8 falls back to int8 pages. int8 has no NaN encoding
— the very same bytes read back as finite integers — and any finite
garbage is neutralized by the additive softmax mask. Double protection,
so the same corruption is asymptomatic there. (The same 0.29→0.30 code
ships on A3; it is harmless there precisely because int8 pages cannot
hold NaN.)

Zeroing after capture restores the clean starting point; it is
semantically safe because these buffers are supposed to be empty at
startup, and runtime page allocations are disjoint from the capture-time
dummy writes.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Startup-time behavior only: persistent buffers are zeroed once after
capture (sub-second, once per engine start).

### How was this patch tested?

- Added `tests/ut/worker/test_zero_static_kv_buffers.py` (CPU): nested
list/tuple/dict structures all zeroed, empty/missing
`static_forward_context` tolerated, fp8 tensors without `zero_()` fall
back to int8 view. 3 passed.
- Manual e2e on 8x Ascend 950DT, GLM-5.3-Flash C8 (TP8+EP, MTP=5,
FULL_DECODE_ONLY, kv-cache fp8, indexer fp8): before the fix, generation
collapses into "!" loops; after the fix, curl sanity check is OK and
GSM8K 1319-question eval reaches 97.27% / 97.73% (two machines),
matching the 0.29.0 baseline 97.88% within run-to-run noise.
- Post-capture state probes: without the fix 73/104 persistent tensors
contain NaN right after capture; with the fix all of them read back
clean.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607
