added.subject: [Doc][Feature] Update the Fine-grained TP guide to align with current support and deployment preconditions (#17968)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Fine-grained TP guide (`Fine_grained_TP.md`) was first added in
#14885 and has since fallen behind the code: lmhead TP (#14668), o_proj
TP (#16967), MLP + embedding TP (#17361), an embedding torch.compile
startup fix (#17903), spec-decode draft-head alignment (#15079, #15495),
and the recompute-scheduler requirement scoped to o_proj/MLP (#17436)
have all landed since. This PR brings the guide back in line with the
behavior on current main, and restructures it along the feature-doc
template (`docs/source/_templates/feature_template.md`):

Content alignment with current main:

- **Models**: state the enforced MoE-only scope — the previous
"model-agnostic / dense architectures" wording contradicted the config
validation. The section now also explains how to check a checkpoint
(`config.json` expert fields: `n_routed_experts` / `num_local_experts` /
`num_experts` / `moe_num_experts` / MoE `block_configs`), why the
restriction exists (fine-grained TP shards across the DP dimension,
which only MoE deployments keep as a cross-rank group), and the exact
startup error text. Dense layers inside a MoE model (e.g. the first
three layers of DeepSeek-R1) remain covered by
`mlp_tensor_parallel_size`.
- **Support matrix**: the `mlp` row now aligns with `o_proj` (graph-mode
decode only). The notes explain the two communication families:
capacity-based exchanges (embedding / LM head) vs uniform-token
exchanges (o_proj / MLP).
- **Preconditions for o_proj / MLP TP**: P/D-disaggregated decode node
(`kv_consumer`), `scheduler_config.recompute_scheduler_enable`,
`PreemptOffloadConnector` combined via `MultiConnector`, graph mode,
`tensor_parallel_size == 1`, `prefill_context_parallel_size == 1`, plus
the capture-bound auto-disable behavior and the runtime eager-step
fail-fast.

Template alignment:

- **Feature Introduction** now carries the quantified benefit summary
and a version statement (v0.30.0 release line).
- New **Usage Scenarios** and **Constraints and Limitations** tables
(template-required) consolidate the scenario/component/precondition
overview.
- Usage examples are split by scenario: a generic embedding + LM head
example, and a full P/D decode-node example enabling **all four knobs
together** (the previous single example combined
`mlp_tensor_parallel_size` with a non-PD launch and fails at config load
on current main).
- New **Verifying the Feature** section (template-required): the
`finegrained_tp_config enabled: ...` startup log line, the capture-bound
auto-disable warning, and a serving check.
- New **Configuration Parameters** table (template-required) for the
four knobs.
- New **FAQs** for the three failure modes a user actually hits
(MoE-only rejection, capture-bound auto-disable, precondition errors).
- Speculative decoding: notes that LM head TP can be combined with
EAGLE, DFlash, and DSpark draft models.

The guide deliberately stays runner-agnostic and does not mention
model-runner versions.

Review follow-ups (from an adversarial doc-vs-code review of this
guide):

- All four knobs currently cannot be combined with pipeline parallelism
(`pipeline_parallel_size > 1`); the underlying group-layout bug is
tracked in #18209.
- The "Standard Tensor Parallelism Requirement" wording for embedding /
LM head is tracked in #18208.
- The Constraints table now also documents the PCP embedding / LM-head
weight-sharding mutex and the not-yet-supported LM head TP ×
speculative-decoding combinations (each fails fast with an explicit
error).
- `additional_config.md`'s example now uses the precondition-free knobs
and links to this guide.

Fixes #18165

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No, documentation-only.

modified file.
- All 12 internal anchor links and the relative link to
`preempt_offload_connector.md` verified programmatically.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Generate the custom AICPU library and registration manifest whenever
`AICPU_CUST_OBJ_TARGETS` is populated, even if `ENABLE_AICPU` was not
set. This is a one-line change to the aggregation condition.

The failure is recorded in [Nightly-A5 run 38170355411,
DeepSeek_V4_Flash_A5 job
114562822896](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/38170355411/job/114562822896),
at source revision `9f9da5562089280a7f01c3d03e855b258e372807`. Decode
FULL graph capture reports `EE1011` / `errno:107000`: kernel
`KvQuantSparseAttnSharedkvMetadata` does not exist. Static inspection of
the digest-pinned test image
`sha256:d1fe99e790ad6772fe4aa61c1c492227d9f99f4c0d7dcf679d8a5d177e271f4b`
confirmed that its custom_transformer vendor tree lacks the entire
`op_impl/cpu` subtree, including `libtransformer_aicpu_kernels.so` and
`cust_aicpu_kernel.json`, while the host ACLNN entry is exported.

`add_aicpu_cust_kernel_modules` registers OBJECT targets and JSON files
but does not set `ENABLE_AICPU`. The legacy `add_modules_sources_aicpu`
macro does set it.
[#18128](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18128) removed
`store_kv_block_metadata` from the A5 build list, removing the remaining
legacy flag-setting path and exposing this implicit dependency. The
aggregate generators already skip empty inputs, so preserving the legacy
flag while also checking registered objects handles both entry paths.

**Why releases/v0.30.0 passes:** [release job
114449695033](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/38127287059/job/114449695033)
used Ascend source `8b9d218cc56d56120da9a9c81626d27a04d8a1f3`, the same
CANN inner version `V100R001C25B114`, FP8 KV and FULL_DECODE_ONLY, and
reported 6 passed. That source still selects `store_kv_block_metadata`,
whose macro enables aggregation. The current release head
`3bf6d2729bcc1e33057fccf90ca0b88041cacaa3` still retains this path. Thus
the release build currently benefits from the legacy side effect; this
fix removes the dependency before the operator is retired there too.
This is a source/log comparison, not a complete binary bisect.

Fixes missing custom AICPU packaging that prevents A5 DeepSeek V4
initialization. No API changes.

aggregation block, existing registration helper and operator CMake:
baseline OBJECT-only case fails as expected; candidate OBJECT-only,
legacy-enabled and no-AICPU cases pass. This checks target generation,
not CANN compilation or device execution.

- `bash format.sh ci` was run in an isolated WSL worktree. All hooks
except typos passed; typos failed with `Cannot allocate memory (os error
12)`. Submission proceeded without waiting for further lint retries at

added.author: freyfwt
added.subject: [BugFix][EPLB] Fix HIXL registration ranges and resource cleanup (#18217)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

HIXL EPLB currently registers whole allocator snapshot segments.
Expandable segments can grow at the same address or release unused
physical pages while their registrations remain active. Main-model and
MoE-draft communicators can also register overlapping aligned ranges
independently.

Give each EPLB state one private HIXL session. After all loading-time
`add_model()` calls, initialize it before starting the existing async
worker. Register the union of the actual expert-weight and
receive-buffer spans across every participating model: align outward to
2 MiB and merge overlapping or adjacent ranges without bridging gaps.
This includes identical starts with different lengths and distinct model
allocations sharing aligned coverage. Pin the original storage until
deregistration succeeds. Each model retains its own layers, slots,
addresses, strides, and READ descriptors. Transfers still access the
original weights and existing expert buffers directly, with no
additional D2D copies or changes to allocation methods.

Validate the ordered model manifest and metadata across ranks before
registration and connection, and reject additions after initialization.
Limit each rank's shared session to 4000 aligned, merged registration
ranges across all participating models. Exceeding the limit fails before
the first local backend registration and uses the existing
initialization rollback. Keep one owner for connections, registered
handles, and submitted requests. Terminal status queries consume backend
request handles, so never query those handles again. Failures anywhere
in the HIXL background migration, including context restoration and the
final stream synchronization, make the entire session unusable.
Foreground checks terminate the worker through the existing RPC
process-death path while preserving registered resources. Unexpected
thread setup failure is fatal too.

Normal shutdown drains the background worker, stops and joins it,
confirms all-rank transfer completion, disconnects peers, deregisters
memory, and finalizes HIXL once. Failed cleanup retains resources and
terminates the worker, including initialization rollback failures
through worker RPC. Cross-thread calls restore the initialization ACL
context, rank confirmations use CPU tensors, and the ctypes MemDesc
matches the CANN reserved-byte layout.

Shared registration ownership stays in `eplb_communicator.py` and
`eplb_state.py`; the existing async-worker wrapper propagates failures
to that owner. A small ctypes destructor guard handles cleared globals
at interpreter shutdown. Setup remains in model loading, before
profiling. Moving registration after profiling/warmup, sleep/wake,
weight reload, model/state replacement, and elastic-EP lifecycle
integration remain outside this PR.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

- EPLB rejects weight offload/prefetch (`cpu_offload_gb > 0` or
`offload_group_size > 0`).
- Failed HIXL transfers or cleanup terminate the worker before
registered resources are released.
- HIXL model registration is sealed before the async worker starts.
- Sessions requiring more than 4000 merged registration ranges fail
initialization.

### How was this patch tested?

Final source commit: `00d4d12434f5edf3823e037202170e36d2ad7b3c`.

- Related CPU tests using repository NPU mocks: **498 passed, 1
skipped**. Covers shared main/draft registration and separate READ
metadata, range union, storage retention, terminal-handle consumption,
failure propagation, ordered model manifests, partial
registration/submission, rollback, basic shutdown, and
worker/controller/config regressions. Tests cover the 4000/4001
registration boundaries, counting merged ranges, and registration-limit
rollback. Context restoration, post-transfer synchronization and thread
setup failures exercise the actual verified upstream RPC handler and
retain both models' shared resources. These tests do not validate NPU
execution.
- `bash format.sh ci`: passed.
- Full `tools/mypy.sh 1` for Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12: passed for
source, examples, and tests against the verified vLLM commit. The local
static environment uses NumPy 1.26 and Triton wheel Python source for
import discovery.
- Expanded real two-device regression:

  ```bash
python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card -q
tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/test_hixl_eplb_registration.py -s
  ```

Includes distinct main/draft storages with overlapping 2 MiB coverage,
one engine/connection set, alternating direct READs after
`empty_cache()` with `expandable_segments=True`, untouched neighboring
bytes, repeat close, same-base 84/86 MiB spans, allocator growth,
background ACL context, the native 4000-registration boundary, and fatal
cleanup/rollback failure injection after real registration.

These standalone HIXL component tests use real torch_npu, ACL and HIXL.
The command avoids the global model-adapter conftest, whose optional
model dependency is unavailable in the test runtime. No NPU or HIXL
stubs were used.

| Hardware | CANN | Binding | Result | Tested commit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ascend A2, earlier 321-region regression | 9.1.0 | ctypes | **4
passed, 2 skipped** (official binding unavailable) | `a0e035c330c8` |
| Ascend A2, earlier 321-region regression | 9.2.0, 2026-09-28 CI image
| official Python and ctypes | **6 passed** | `dd4656b5c8e9` |
| Ascend A3, 4000-region boundary | 9.1.0 | ctypes | **4 passed, 2
skipped** (official binding unavailable) | `00d4d12434f5` |
| Ascend A3, 4000-region boundary | 9.2.0 CI image | official Python and
ctypes | **6 passed** | `00d4d12434f5` |

The A2 rows describe the earlier 321-region implementation. The final
4000-region limit is validated on A3. Independent review of the final
source and worker-RPC failure boundary found no remaining P1/P2 source
blockers. The CI duration entry for this new test is also present; the
local workflow coverage check passes.

**A5 hardware coverage, full-model acceptance, and steady-state
performance acceptance remain outstanding.** Component transfer timings
are diagnostics, not end-to-end performance evidence. Ready for review;
the outstanding acceptance items above remain documented for merge
assessment.

added.subject: [BugFix][KVTransfer] Keep AscendStore receive registration until completion (#16461)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #16460.

When a request is aborted while waiting for an asynchronous AscendStore
load, the core scheduler retains its KV blocks until receive completion.
AscendStore currently removes the request from `_loading_req_ids` when
it sees `finished_req_ids`. The worker filters receive completions
against that set, so the completion is never reported and the deferred
release cannot finish.

Keep the receive registration across request termination, and clear it
through the existing `update_finished_recving()` method when connector
output reports completion. This also clears registrations after normal
receives. The scheduler's ownership assertions, worker completion filter
and preemption cleanup remain unchanged.

Rebased onto upstream `c2fa1a926` as a single signed-off commit. The
receive-registration fix and four regression tests are unchanged by the
rebase (`git range-diff` reports an equivalent patch). The PR changes
only the scheduler and its unit tests.

Related work: #14132 addresses load/save co-queueing. #16119 removes the
synchronous-save delayed-free handshake but leaves this
receive-registration path unchanged. This change addresses missing
receive completion, distinct from the late notification for an
already-removed request described in vllm-project/vllm#43226.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Aborted requests can complete their deferred KV-block release after
asynchronous AscendStore loads finish. No API or configuration changes.

### How was this patch tested?

Current revision (`17f051039`, upstream `c2fa1a926`):

- `git diff --check`, Python syntax parsing, Ruff lint and formatting
passed. The repository `format.sh ci` checks passed except for two local

bodies and the four existing regression tests with explicit test state
and a lightweight connector-output stub. All four tests passed on the
rebased PR; the upstream implementation still triggered regression
assertions. This does not exercise full imports, scheduler
initialization, real block-pool accounting, storage I/O or device DMA.
- Full CPU and device checks on this revision are pending GitHub CI; the
local macOS environment does not have torch/vLLM installed.

Previous revision (`501e9668`, upstream `bea70ab8`, verified vLLM
dependency `ced6857`), not a rerun on the rebased revision:

38200018603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/38200018603)

added.subject: [BugFix][SpecDecode] Disable compilation for eager drafts (#18462)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

MRV2 already disables draft ACL graph capture when
`speculative_config.enforce_eager` is true, but the draft still inherits
the target's compilation mode. This can trigger npugraph_ex static
kernel compilation after startup when a new draft input size is first
executed.

Give eager drafts shallow copies of `VllmConfig` and `CompilationConfig`
in `init_speculator`, and set the draft compilation mode to `NONE`. The
target keeps its compilation settings, while the layer registries remain
shared. Existing draft graph-mode handling is retained.

This compatibility fix can be removed once all supported vLLM versions
handle eager draft compilation in the common speculator construction
path used by Ascend.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Explicitly eager MRV2 drafts no longer enter the model compilation
backend. No new configuration options are introduced.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added a parameterized factory test for
`enforce_eager=True/False/None`, target configuration isolation, and
shared layer registries. The new eager case failed before the fix.

added.author: tyy0829
added.subject: [main][Bugfix][KV Pool] Drop save-side GVA cache on idempotent batch_alloc (#18353)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Supersedes #18253.

MemCache has confirmed that `batch_alloc` is now **idempotent**: calling
it on an existing key safely returns the blob's current GVA,
re-registered in the client-side SDK tracker, with a lease. The
constraint that forced the layerwise save path to keep a cross-step
`_allocated_gvas` account book no longer exists, and neither do the bugs
it caused:

- wrong-address `batch_copy` writes through stale cached GVAs after
DRAM/SSD demote-rewarm cycles (the issue #18253 patched at the metadata
level)
- `-3102` unregistered-GVA failures on reused destinations (the
client-side registration issue; fresh allocations are always registered
+ leased)

This PR removes the cache and makes the save path **stateless per
step**:

1. Blocks already committed in the pool are skipped through a
medium-agnostic `batch_is_exist` filter (`_pool_keys_missing`). Skipping
only needs data presence: a block committed on any medium does not need
re-saving, and the load path (`_prepare_load_gvas` ->
`batch_get_key_info(for_load=True)`) rewarms SSD blocks on read. The
filter reuses `_step_exist_cache` for per-step dedup and **fails open**
(check errors are treated as missing), so an unreadable pool costs
transfer bandwidth, never the blocks themselves.
2. Every transferred block is allocated fresh via `batch_alloc` in the
same step, so write targets are always current, client-registered and
leased. This also renews leases every step instead of relying on an
allocation-time TTL across steps.
3. Partial keys keep their request-scoped fresh allocation.
4. Removed: the `_allocated_gvas` dict, `_refresh_allocated_gvas`, the
cache-membership prefix skip, the hole GVA reuse and the
unbounded-growth concern of a never-cleared dict.

Net save-path RPC cost per step is unchanged versus the original design
(one exists batch + one alloc batch), and the keyinfo/lease
double-validation added by #18253 is gone.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API/config change. Requires a MemCache deployment whose `batch_alloc`
is idempotent (confirmed with the MemCache team; deployments with the
old `MMC_DUPLICATED_OBJECT` behavior are no longer supported by this
path).

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests updated/added in `tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/`:
- `test_pool_worker.py`:
`test_committed_blocks_are_skipped_and_missing_blocks_allocated` (new,
replaces the cache-based realloc test),
`test_exists_check_failure_fails_open_and_transfers_all` (new); test
helpers default `batch_is_exist` to all-missing so existing GVA save
tests exercise the fresh-alloc path
- `test_glm53_store.py`: null-KDA-slot membership assertion moved from
`_allocated_gvas` to `request.save_keys`
- `python -m py_compile`, `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass locally.
- UT run on an NPU dev container to follow (`pytest -sv
tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py
tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_glm53_store.py`); will update
with results.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8cc9aa5ad350f6f80cf3bebb298d410803ff75a9

added.subject: [BugFix][MoE] Preserve MiniMax-M3 prequantized shared Down input (#18396)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

MiniMax-M3 on Ascend A5 with W8A8-MXFP8 shared experts can return a
pre-quantized `(activation, scale)` tuple from its SwiGLU-OAI
activation. With shared-expert multistream overlap enabled,
`_prepare_linear_input_for_overlap` passes that tuple into
`prepare_input_for_overlap`, which assumes a Tensor and calls `x.dim()`.
This causes `AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'dim'`
(seen in [this nightly
job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/38200792613/job/114654898426)).

Accept the existing `LinearInput` contract at the overlap preparation
boundary. Already-prepared inputs pass unchanged to the registered Down
projection, preserving the quantized tensor and scale without a second
quantization. Plain Tensor inputs still use the scheme-owned early
preparation path. Add a regression test that exercises the
linear-wrapper Down stage with a tuple activation and verifies the
scheme is not called again.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It prevents this MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 multistream path from failing
during model execution. No CLI or API changes.

added.author: zhaoting
added.subject: [Performance][MoE] Optimize NPU event recording for MoE multistream overlap (#17603)
added.body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The NPU events recorded around the routed-experts path (router milestones `shared_input_ready`/`router_output_ready`, and `before_dispatch`/`before_gmm2`/`before_combine` inside the routed path) are consumed **only** by the shared-expert side stream, which exists solely when `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` is enabled. When the overlap is off, every `record_event` is pure host-side overhead paid per MoE layer per step, and host-side record is notably slow. The consumers in `shared_experts.py` already gate every wait on the same flag (`_wait_for_milestone` returns immediately when the overlap is off and fails fast if a milestone is missing while it is on), and the `RoutedMoEMilestones`/`FusedExpertsResult` event fields are already `Optional`. So the producer-side records can be skipped safely with no consumer changes. This PR gates the always-on-path record sites behind the flag via a shared helper, `maybe_record_event()` (defined in `ops/fused_moe/moe_mlp.py`): - `ops/fused_moe/moe_mlp.py`: define `maybe_record_event()` and use it for the `before_gmm2_evt` record in `apply_moe_mlp`; the entry now returns an Optional event; - `ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py`: gate `before_dispatch_evt` / `before_combine_evt`; - `ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`: gate `shared_input_ready` / `router_output_ready` in `_prepare_router_and_milestones` (`routed_finalize_done` is already recorded only on the SP-overlap gather path, so it needs no extra gating). `maybe_record_event()` skips the record only when the initialized config proves the overlap is off; an uninitialized config keeps the legacy always-record behavior. The 310P-specific and LoRA gmm2 records are intentionally left unconditional for now (not yet validated on device); they can adopt the same gate in a follow-up. With the overlap off (default), the main MoE path no longer issues any event records; with the overlap on, behavior is unchanged. ### Profiling Host-side timeline of one MoE layer step before and after this change: **Before (events recorded unconditionally on the routed stream):** **After (records skipped when multistream overlap is off):** ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. With `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` enabled the behavior is unchanged; with it disabled only the unused event records are skipped. ### How was this patch tested? - The runner-contract unit tests (`tests/ut/ops/test_fused_moe.py`) patch the overlap flag explicitly to keep exercising the record path, and new cases cover the skip path (milestones stay `None` with `record_event` never called); all other MoE tests (including 310P and LoRA) run unchanged. - CPU UT / pre-commit / DCO checks on this PR. - E2E MoE serving on Ascend NPU with `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` off (skip path) and on (unchanged path), plus the profiling screenshots above. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607 Signed-off-by: zhao_ting_v Co-authored-by: zhao_ting_v

added.author: wzk-jazk
added.subject: [BugFix][Scheduler] Adapt vllm#49675 deferred-free preemption guard to DyntraLB and Balance schedulers (#18207)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

vllm-project/vllm#49675 (included in vLLM v0.30.0) fixed a zero-progress
preemption cascade in `Scheduler.schedule()`. With deferred block
freeing (`defer_block_free`, enabled by async scheduling or PP > 1 plus
a KV-consumer connector), a preempted request's blocks return to the
pool only after its in-flight step is processed. When an allocation
fails, preempting such a request cannot free anything this step, so the
retry loop preempted the whole running queue while the free-block count
stayed 0 (see #16315). Upstream now selects the victim first and stops
retrying when `_request_blocks_can_be_freed()` is false.

vllm-ascend keeps its own copies of `schedule()`. The recompute and
profiling-chunk schedulers already received this change while syncing to
v0.30.0 (#17672, #17380), and `DyntraLBRecomputeScheduler` inherits it
from `RecomputeScheduler`. Two copies are still missing it:

- `DyntraLBScheduler` / `AsyncDyntraLBScheduler`
(`vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py`). DyntraLB requires
`kv_role="kv_consumer"`, so deferred freeing is on in every async
DyntraLB deployment and the cascade is hit whenever the KV pool is full.
- `BalanceScheduler`
(`vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py`), used on the
sync path; affected with PP > 1 and a `kv_both` connector (which vLLM
treats as a KV consumer).

This PR ports the upstream guard to both, with the same structure as
upstream and `RecomputeScheduler`: select the victim, stop retrying if
its blocks cannot be freed this step, and only then remove it from the
running queue. No other part of the copied `schedule()` bodies is
changed; fully re-syncing `BalanceScheduler.schedule()` with v0.30.0 is
left as separate maintenance work.

Refs #16315. Related: #16265, which addresses the same issue by patching
in a full copy of upstream `Scheduler.schedule()` with the guard; it was
opened before the v0.30.0 upgrade, and upstream `Scheduler` now carries
the fix itself. This PR only covers the `schedule()` copies that
vllm-ascend still maintains.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

New unit tests, modeled on upstream's
`tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py` from vllm#49675:

- `tests/ut/core/test_dyntra_lb_scheduler.py`
-
`test_dyntra_lb_allocation_retry_waits_for_fence_then_succeeds[fcfs|priority]`:
port of upstream `test_allocation_retry_waits_for_fence_then_succeeds`.
While the victim is in flight the step preempts nothing; after the fence
advances, the expected victim is preempted and the trigger request is
scheduled.
- `test_dyntra_lb_full_pool_does_not_cascade_preempt_on_deferred_free`:
the KV pool is full and the previous step is still in flight. Without
the fix all running requests are preempted with 0 free blocks; with it
none are, and the next step matches upstream `AsyncScheduler`.
- `tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_balance_schedule.py`
-
`test_balance_allocation_retry_waits_for_fence_then_succeeds[fcfs|priority]`:
the same scenario on the sync path, where PP overlap is reproduced by
scheduling the next prefill chunk before the previous step's output is
processed.
- `test_balance_full_pool_does_not_cascade_preempt_on_deferred_free`: no
cascade while a chunked prefill needs blocks and every other request is
in flight; the next step matches upstream `Scheduler` (balance
disabled).
- `_make_balance_scheduler` gains optional `policy` and `num_blocks`
arguments; existing callers are unchanged.

All six new tests fail without the fix. The full
`test_dyntra_lb_scheduler.py`, `test_patch_balance_schedule.py`,
`test_dyntra_lb_recompute_scheduler.py` and
`test_recompute_scheduler.py` pass
(`test_schedule_body_matches_pinned_release_tag` is skipped as before
this change, since the Balance copy already differed from v0.30.0).

added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Long sequences or high concurrency can exceed the default 480-second
Mooncake KV-cache release timeout. Add guidance to both single-node and
multi-node PD tutorials to increase the timeout to 1800 seconds (30
minutes) when needed.

Explain that increasing the timeout generally does not affect inference
accuracy or normal-operation performance, but delays releasing pending
KV caches when a decoder fails, temporarily reducing available HBM on
the prefiller. Distinguish the older `VLLM_MOONCAKE_CONNECTOR_TIMEOUT`
setting from the current `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` name.

No. Documentation only; no runtime behavior changes.

added.author: Tjh-UKN
added.subject: [MRV2][Feature][msprobe] Add direct msprobe dump support to model runner v2 (#16125)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

msprobe-based accuracy data dump is currently wired only into the v1
`NPUModelRunner`. When serving with model runner v2
(`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`), the existing
`--additional-config '{"dump_config": ...}'` (or `dump_config_path`)
options silently produce no dump data, so the msprobe accuracy-debugging
workflow cannot be used on v2.

This PR ports the same instrumentation to the v2 `NPUModelRunner`,
driven by the identical `AscendConfig` fields — no new flags and no DFX
involvement:

- `__init__`: create `PrecisionDebugger` for eager mode
  (`cudagraph_mode == NONE`) or `AclGraphDumper` for aclgraph modes,
  only when a dump config is present (no msprobe dependency otherwise).
- `load_model`: start the dumper before aclgraph capture (v1 parity:
  v1 starts it at the end of `load_model`).
- `execute_model`: open the dump window for real steps and
  scheduler-driven dummy runs
  (`dump_forward = dummy_run or total_num_scheduled_tokens > 0`), then
  close it with `dump=False` for dummy runs, and close it for PP
  non-last ranks (which return `IntermediateTensors` and never reach
  `sample_tokens`).
- `sample_tokens`: close the per-step dump cycle on the normal
  last-PP-rank path (`start -> forward -> stop -> step`).
- `_start_dump_data` / `_finalize_dump_data` helpers, identical to v1.

Beyond a literal port, two insertion points are adapted to the v2
architecture, where the engine only calls `sample_tokens` when
`execute_model` returns `None`, and the worker routes pooling to
`pool()`:

1. **Pooling models**: in v2 the worker calls `model_runner.pool()`
   instead of `sample_tokens`, so the dump cycle is closed in a
   `pool()` override (v1 parity: v1 finalizes after `_pool()`).
   Without this, dumping a pooling model would never reach `step()`.
2. **Internal `_dummy_run` calls**: `profile_run` (including the MC2
   dummy) and memory-profiling forwards bypass `execute_model` and call
   `_dummy_run` directly. v1 flushes the dump window with
   `_finalize_dump_data(dump=False)` at the end of every `_dummy_run`;
   the same flush is added here, otherwise capture/profiling forwards
   leak into the first real step's dump data and shift step numbering.

Known limitation: EC transfer (encoder-only ranks) has an explicit dump
branch in v1, but EC transfer is not yet supported by model runner v2
in vllm-ascend; when it lands, the encoder-only path will need the same
start/finalize treatment.

The approach follows @djh95's `feat/decouple-msprobe-dfx` branch,
rebased onto current main and extended with the two v2-specific fixes
above.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: msprobe dump now works with model runner v2 through the existing
`dump_config` / `dump_config_path` additional-config options. No new
CLI/API surface, and behavior is unchanged when no dump config is set.

### How was this patch tested?

- Insertion points were cross-checked against the v1 call sites in
  `model_runner_v1.py` and the vllm v2 engine/worker call flow
  (`execute_model` -> optional `pool()` -> `sample_tokens` only on
  `None` return).
- Manual verification steps on NPU:
  1. Eager mode: `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <model>
     --additional-config '{"dump_config": {"task": "statistics",
     "level": "L1", "dump_path": "/data/msprobe_dump", "statistics":
     {"list": []}}}'`, send a few requests, verify
     `dump_path/step*/rank*/dump.json` is produced per step.
  2. aclgraph mode (default cudagraph mode): same command, verify
     `AclGraphDumper` writes per-step data (requires msprobe built with
     `aclgraph_dump` enabled).
  3. PP=2: verify non-last ranks also produce one dump step per
     scheduler step.
- CI.

added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Replace the plugin-owned quantized Lightning Indexer (QLI) with the CANN
operator exposed by `torch_npu.npu_quant_lightning_indexer`, removing
the duplicate kernel implementation and its build and Torch registration
paths.

- Switch the base device adaptor's QLI path to the native operator. Pass
`INT64_MAX` for `pre_tokens` and `next_tokens` in both the base and A5
paths; A5 already used the native operator.
- Remove `csrc/attention/lightning_indexer_quant`, its build entries,
and the `_C_ascend.npu_lightning_indexer_quant` binding and meta
implementation.
- Update the SFA unit test to check the native call and token-window
arguments, and migrate the fused quantized Lightning Indexer management
test's reference call.
- Keep the custom MoeGatingTopK implementation, build entries, bindings,
device adaptor behavior, and tests identical to the PR base.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The QLI path now uses the CANN operator through `torch_npu`. The device
adaptor interface is unchanged. Direct callers of the removed private
`torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_lightning_indexer_quant` schema must migrate to
`torch_npu.npu_quant_lightning_indexer`.

### How was this patch tested?

Validation after restoring MoeGatingTopK (October 12), against vLLM
`8cc9aa5ad350f6f80cf3bebb298d410803ff75a9`:

- Device adaptor and SFA unit tests: **132 passed**.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks: passed for the five relevant Python
files.
- `git diff --check b59bfc57c...HEAD`: passed.
- Confirmed the restored MoE kernel directory and tests match the PR
base byte-for-byte, and all device adaptor MoE gating methods match the
base.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but interrupted while
installing the actionlint environment; the complete hook suite has not
passed locally.
- NPU integration tests and the extension build were not rerun for this
scope reduction.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pr16731-qli-vllm-verified python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/device/test_device_op.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_v1.py --maxfail=1
# 132 passed
```

Historical QLI validation (recorded before the September 23 rebase, not
rerun for this scope reduction): the extension build and
DeepSeek-V3.2-W8A8 TP16 inference with LI C8 enabled succeeded on CANN
9.2.0-beta.2, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, and Ascend 910B4-1.

### QLI kernel performance comparison

Historical eager-mode profiling on CANN 9.2.0-beta.2 and Ascend 910B4-1
used isolated old/native processes, 50 warmups, and 20 profiler samples
per case. Across 19 eligible QLI cases, the old/native median kernel
durations were `24.98 us / 22.87 us`. Representative results were `19.99
us / 15.38 us` at the 128-token block boundary and `42.94 us / 41.70 us`
for the long sparse case. Two non-64-head cases were excluded because
the old kernel raised an AICore address/UB error. These are kernel-only
measurements; no graph capture/replay performance claim is made.

added.subject: [BugFix][Ops] Include SparseFlashAttention in A5 custom kernel builds (#18258)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add `sparse_flash_attention` to the Ascend950 custom ACLNN operator
build list. A5 builds currently omit this operator, so the DCP LSE fixes
from #16656 can be present in source while runtime still executes the
CANN built-in kernel.

On the tested CANN 9.2.0 image, this also causes an input ABI mismatch:
the repository custom host has nine inputs, while the selected built-in
kernel declares ten, including optional `sinks`. Kernel metadata and
runtime logs confirm this mismatch. The first model request fails with
illegal GM access; installing the matching existing custom kernel
resolves it. The CANN kernel runs correctly through its compatible
`torch_npu` interface.

The existing build/install pipeline can then include the repository's
SFA implementation in subsequent A5 packages and images. The final diff
is one line in `csrc/build_aclnn.sh`; kernel sources, dependencies and
tests are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Ascend950 builds with custom kernel compilation enabled will include the
repository's SFA implementation. Existing images require rebuilding.
There is no public API change.

### How was this patch tested?

The final source tree is identical to the previously validated
build-only commit `84606e6bbac76e5c6361b717654198a17071f9cb`. The
following results concern the existing repository implementation, not
the CANN source import:

- `git diff <base> --check` and `bash -n csrc/build_aclnn.sh` passed.
- On Ascend950DT, CANN 9.2.0, torch 2.10.0 and torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, a
clean SFA build and installation succeeded using current main's
`buffer.h`, without an additional attention-buffer include. All 12
padded-index/empty-shard regression configurations passed in 1.86
seconds. Runtime evidence confirmed selection of the custom kernel.
- Normal-input precision matrix: 80/80 custom configurations passed
independent CPU FP64 reference checks. Covers FP16/BF16, TND/PA_BSND KV,
LSE on/off, 1/4 query tokens, 128/512/2048 selected keys and two seeds.
All 60 CANN-supported attention outputs and all 20 comparable LSE
results were exactly equal to custom results, with maximum absolute
difference 0. CANN rejected the 20 PA_BSND + LSE configurations.
- Padded-index/empty-shard matrix: all 20 LSE-enabled custom
configurations passed the reference. The 20 LSE-disabled padded
configurations produced outputs exactly equal to CANN but both
implementations failed the independent reference; these existing cases
are outside the LSE-gated fix and are not counted as correctness passes.
- Real GLM-5.2 first-layer causal input (20 query tokens, 8 heads, BF16,
PA_BSND): custom output passes a CPU FP64 reference with LSE off/on
(maximum absolute error 0.00792033, atol=0.03/rtol=0.01); LSE maximum
absolute error is 4.425e-7. With LSE off, all 81,920 output elements
exactly match correctly invoked CANN, maximum absolute difference 0.
- In the A5 image
`dev-26.2.0.day20261009-A5-py311-openEuler24.03-lts-aarch64`, the full
GLM-5.2 W4A8 model with BF16 KV successfully answers a smoke request
after installing the existing custom SFA. Runtime logs confirm the
custom kernel selection; 23 native source/header files match the final
PR tree.
- Per user-requested scope, evaluated official GSM8K test IDs 0..499
with the full GLM-5.2 W4A8 model, BF16 KV, TP8, concurrency 64,
temperature 0 and seed 1024. Custom DCP1: 488/500 (97.6%); custom DCP8:
481/500 (96.2%). Both have zero request errors and zero truncations.
Independent text-only rescoring agrees. No mojibake, empty outputs or
abnormal repetition were detected. DCP1/DCP8 differ on 12 final
numerical answers; the 1.4 percentage-point score difference is
recorded, not claimed as equivalence.
- A valid model-level CANN baseline was not established. The initial
adapter still resolved the image custom host; selectively forwarding SFA
API resolution to CANN avoided the input ABI mismatch, but the model
produced abnormal text. That attempt was stopped and excluded from
accuracy comparisons; its remaining cause is unresolved. Operator-level
exact-match evidence above is separate and does not establish
model-level CANN parity. Test adapters/bridges are not in this PR. The
earlier interrupted 748-response full-test run remains archived.
- Full-list A5 compilation of the #16656 source snapshot encountered
failures in other operators, including ChunkGatedDeltaRuleFwdH and
causal_conv1d. This does not establish a successful full-image build.
- Local full `bash format.sh ci` was initially blocked by an actionlint
installation network error. GitHub pre-commit and both CPU unit-test
jobs subsequently passed. The CI gate requires a maintainer testing
label before precision/full CI can run; this is still pending.

Validation covers the fixed 500-question subset, not all 1319 GSM8K
questions or model-level CANN precision equivalence, and does not
establish a successful full-image build; it does not cover performance,
quantized SFA inputs, sinks or all attention modes. Evaluation adapters
and tracing are isolated test harness changes, not part of this one-line
PR.

added.author: Akine-Ko
added.subject: [Feature][EC Connector] Support encoder cache CPU offloading on Ascend (#13894)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it

Depends on vllm-project/vllm#54033.

This PR adds Ascend support for the upstream `ECCPUConnector`, enabling
multimodal encoder-cache offloading to CPU shared memory.

#### Architecture

The implementation keeps the common ECCPU design in upstream vLLM:

- `ECCPUConnector` metadata and role handling;
- `ECCPUScheduler`, `EmbeddingCache`, and `ECSharedRegion`;
- descriptor construction and contiguous-block coalescing;
- common save/load batching, stream and Event lifetime, completion
polling, and worker metadata;
- common shared-mmap cleanup.

`AscendECCPUConnector` registers an Ascend implementation under the
standard `ECCPUConnector` name. `AscendECCPUWorker` inherits the
upstream worker and supplies the Ascend backend through the three
extension points introduced by vLLM PR #54033:

- `_pin_shared_region()` registers the shared mmap as pinned Host memory
through CANN;
- `_submit_transfer()` submits batched D2H and H2D copies through CANN;
- `_shutdown_transfer_backend()` synchronizes the NPU and unregisters
the pinned mmap.

The Ascend worker also creates NPU timing Events, releases transfer
resources safely after asynchronous completion, and restores its save
state after submission failures. Availability of the required CANN
Host-registration and batched-copy APIs is validated before enabling
offload.

Worker Event completion reports drive the scheduler-side cache state: a
completed D2H save marks an entry ready, while completed H2D loads
release its scheduler pin.

#### Model Runner support

ECCPU supports Model Runner V2 only.

Refs #13057.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. Users running Model Runner V2 can enable encoder-cache CPU
offloading on Ascend with:

```python
ECTransferConfig(
    ec_connector="ECCPUConnector",
    ec_role="ec_both",
    ec_connector_extra_config={
        "ec_cpu_bytes": 4294967296,
    },
)
```

The same configuration can be passed to the server CLI:

```bash
--ec-transfer-config \
'{"ec_connector":"ECCPUConnector","ec_role":"ec_both","ec_connector_extra_config":{"ec_cpu_bytes":4294967296}}'
```

### How was this patch tested?

#### Model Runner V2 E2E validation

The single-NPU ECCPU E2E test passed with Model Runner V2, covering the
cold encoder path, D2H cache save, and subsequent H2D cache load.

#### Model Runner V2 performance comparison

A same-device baseline/ECCPU comparison was performed with Model Runner
V2:

- dataset: 500 images from the Open Images V7 validation set;
- compressed image size: approximately 450–550 KiB per image;
- access pattern: the same 500 unique images repeated for 5 sequential
passes;
- 2,500 requests per run;
- maximum concurrency: 10;
- output length: 100 tokens;
- temperature: 0;
- prefix caching: disabled;

added.subject: [BugFix][310P] fix Qwen3.5-2B-w8a8 performance issue on the 310P (#18390)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
On Ascend 310P MRV2, #17278 restored Qwen3.5-2B MTP decode performance
by skipping empty updatable-graph handshakes and avoiding redundant D2H
syncs on the FULL ACLGraph path. Later #17461 remapped MTP verify
attention state from `SpecDecoding` to `ChunkedPrefill` in shared
helpers (validated on 910-class devices, not on 310P). The 310P eager
gate still treats any non-`SpecDecoding` MTP batch as unsafe for FULL
replay, so every uniform MTP step was forced to `CUDAGraphMode.NONE`.
That erased the #17278 gains and regressed 2B-W8A8 decode by ~3× (TPOT
~64ms / ~15 tok/s vs ~22ms / ~45 tok/s) even though draft acceptance
stayed healthy.

This PR is scoped to `_310p` only: promote uniform MTP verify back to
`SpecDecoding` for InputBatch + the eager gate (MRv1 parity), align
draft-prefill metadata with SpecDecoding capture, and resolve the GDN
chunk FwdH op under both pre-/post-#17997 symbol names for stale
extensions.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No. No new public APIs or config knobs. Behavior change is limited to
Ascend 310P MRV2 speculative decoding / GDN chunk-op symbol resolution.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit: tests/ut/_310p/test_model_runner_v2_310p.py (SpecDecoding
promote + eager gate); tests/ut/_310p/spec_decode/test_mtp_mrv2_310.py
(draft-prefill SpecDecoding).

- E2E (310P, NPU, VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1, IO=1024, TP1, BS1, 4
prompts, --no-enable-prefix-caching):

Qwen3.5-2B-W8A8 MTP: TPOT 22.7 ms, output 43.1 tok/s (was ~63.6 ms /
~15.6 tok/s).
Same setup no MTP: TPOT 21.9 ms, output 44.6 tok/s (MTP ≈ no-MTP; no
severe MTP regression).

Other testing results for Qwen3.5-w8a8(MRv2) on the 310P:

added.subject: [BugFix][310P] Fix W8A8SC ND activations and sharded-state save (#18542)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

- `npu_matmul_compress_dequant` only accepts 2D activations. Vision
towers pass `[B, S, K]` into W8A8SC linear, so flatten before the kernel
and restore the leading dimensions on the output.
- `examples/save_sharded_state_310.py` built the engine from
`dataclasses.asdict(EngineArgs)`, which keeps nested `None` defaults
that pydantic `CompilationConfig` rejects. Those `None` values are now
dropped before constructing the LLM.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

W8A8SC linear on 310P now accepts activations with more than two
dimensions, which unblocks vision-tower layers. The 310 sharded-state
save script can start when `EngineArgs` contains nested `None` defaults.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added
`tests/ut/_310p/quantization/test_w8a8sc_310.py::TestAscendW8A8SCLinearMethod310.test_apply_reshapes_nd_activation_310`
to cover flattening `[B, S, K]` and restoring `[B, S, N]`.
- The save-script change is a local argument filter around `LLM`
construction and was not covered by an automated test.

added.author: wangxiyuan
added.subject: [Misc] drop patch_dp_device_ids patch and unify DP device selection (#16601)
added.body:
Remove the v0.24.0-era monkeypatch of
get_physical_gpu_ids_for_local_dp_rank. The patch tolerated a
pre-sharded ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES env var, but that is not the
upstream contract after vllm#45026: vLLM slices the un-sharded env (or
the full --device-ids list) per DP rank itself. The patch silently
turned device misconfiguration into a successful-looking startup and
replaced upstream error context with a raw IndexError.

- Delete vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_dp_device_ids.py and its
  registration and documentation entry.
- tests/e2e/conftest.py: pass the full un-sharded device_ids list for
  every executor backend in _run_vllm_runner_dp_worker, so vLLM's
  per-rank slicing never relies on the env var offset. The Ray branch
  still pre-slices ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES per DP rank because each
  DP worker starts its own local Ray instance, which must only see its
  own NPUs; otherwise independent Ray instances can bind two ranks to
  the same physical NPU (HCCL EI0015). The full device_ids is passed
  alongside, so the pre-sharded env needs no patch.

Migration:
- Affected: application-level DP that pre-shards
  ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES per rank without passing --device-ids.
  Ranks > 0 now fail fast with the upstream "Error computing device
  indices ..." message instead of silently using wrong devices.
- Fix: stop pre-sharding the env and let vLLM slice the full device
  list per DP rank, or pass the full device list via --device-ids /
  LLM(device_ids=[...]).
- Ray: if the env is pre-sharded per DP rank, also pass the full
device_ids; single-server Ray DP scheduling does not need env sharding.
- Unaffected: single-instance serving, one process per DP instance, and
  setups that already pass device_ids.

---

added.author: chenxi-hh
added.subject: [Performance][Model] Offload Qwen3.5-VL image preprocessing to NPU (#16996)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Qwen3.5-VL image preprocessing (resize, patchify, rescale+normalize)
runs on the front-end CPU and saturates the API-server process under
multimodal load, slowing down the engine loop.

Add Ascend subclasses of Qwen3.5-VL (dense and MoE) that move the whole
pipeline onto the NPU worker: the front-end emits flat raw uint8 plus
the original (H, W) and the target grid; the model performs resize
(bicubic+antialias, matching HF/PIL), patchify, and normalization (via
FusedInputNorm) on the device. The front-end-to-worker payload drops ~8x
(uint8, no temporal replication). smart_resize stays on the CPU so
placeholder accounting and prompt lengths are unchanged.

Video keeps the CPU patchify path; only rescale+normalize move to the
device via the native supports_mm_device_do_normalize mechanism.

Registered through ModelRegistry (architecture overwrite, same pattern
as AscendDeepseekV4ForConditionalGeneration in #15457); no vllm or
transformers class is monkey-patched.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. On Ascend, Qwen3.5-VL images are preprocessed on the NPU instead of
the front-end CPU. No config change required; outputs are numerically
equivalent.

### How was this patch tested?

- NPU e2e on Qwen3.5-VL 27B BF16: image-text requests succeed with
correct outputs.
- Numerical comparison with stock path: ViT output cosine similarity
~0.999996 (bicubic+antialias reproduces HF/PIL resize).
- Non-Qwen3.5 model regression: qwen2.5-vl routes to the native vllm
class, behavior unchanged.
- Front-end CPU utilization significantly reduced under multimodal load.

### How was this patch tested?

accuracy :

MMMU：81.11

10K input, 300 output with images
performance :
Output token throughput (tok/s)：104 -> 116
TTFT: 2221ms-> 1914ms

### What this PR does / why we need it?

A5 SFA C8 decode context parallelism needs quantized KV block transport
and per-shard softmax statistics. The previous capability guard rejects
this configuration; the CANN C8 path does not provide the LSE statistics
needed to merge DCP shards.

This patch preserves packed FP8 bytes during block selection and
communication, routes A5 C8 LSE requests to
`KvQuantSparseFlashAttentionVllm`, and returns softmax max/sum with
correct padded-index and empty-shard handling. It registers the A5 C8
DCP capability while retaining platform validation. RoPE64 calls without
LSE keep the CANN path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. A5 sparse attention with FP8 KV cache can use decode context
parallelism. Model weight quantization is unchanged, and no new CLI flag
is added. SFA C8 is derived from the KV cache dtype and sparse model
configuration.

### How was this patch tested?

- Built the standard A5 wheel with `COMPILE_CUSTOM_KERNELS=1`; verified
six C8 kernel binaries and matching metadata in the package.

- A5: the existing operator test file passed all 13 cases after review
consolidation (the original case plus 12 A5 LSE cases): 16/32/64 heads
with complete, padded, and empty selections. Padded outputs were checked

completed a real arithmetic decode correctly. The same PR wheel was

Full-model GSM8K comparison (same 500 questions, prompt, seed 1024,
temperature 0, and max output 2048): GLM-5.2 MXFP8 weights, FP8 KV/SFA
C8, MRV2, TP8 x PP2 with a 38/40 layer partition, FULL_DECODE_ONLY
graphs, and request concurrency 64.

| Metric | DCP1 | DCP8 within each PP stage |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Correct answers | 482/500 | 484/500 |

DCP8 improved aggregate accuracy by 0.4 percentage points: 7 questions

added.author: LeiW777
added.subject: [BugFix][Model] Patch MiniMax-M3 fused all-reduce norm on vLLM's real module instead of shadowing it (#18543)
added.body:
## Summary

On Ascend A3 with the B097 image, `MiniMax-M3` + mooncake KV pooling
failed to start with:

```
ImportError: cannot import name '_AR_RESIDUAL_RMS_NORM' from 'vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm' (unknown location)
```

Root cause: `_install_fused_allreduce_norm_fallback()` created a fake
`ModuleType` named
`vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm` and injected
it into `sys.modules`, shadowing vLLM's real module. The fake module
only exposes the single entry `fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm`, so any
consumer importing vLLM-internal symbols from that module — e.g. kimi_k3
DSpark's top-level `from
vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm import
_AR_RESIDUAL_RMS_NORM` — fails with the ImportError above ("unknown
location" = the fake module has no source file). Shadowing the real
module also couples vllm-ascend to upstream private symbols and affects
every importer of that module.

## Changes

`vllm_ascend/models/minimax_m3/minimax_m3_vl.py` (only file touched):

- Drop `import sys`, `from types import ModuleType`, `from typing import
Any, cast` — they existed solely for the fake-module mechanism.
- `_install_fused_allreduce_norm_fallback()` now imports vLLM's **real**
module
(`import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm as
_real`)
and replaces only its public entry
`_real.fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm` with the Ascend implementation
(SP-MoE `reduce_scatter` + `all_reduce` + `GemmaRMSNorm`).
- The SP-MoE function body is unchanged; no fake module, no
`sys.modules` injection, no internal-symbol mirroring.

## Why

- **Independence from upstream internals** — only the public API entry
is patched. If upstream renames or changes its private symbols,
vllm-ascend does not have to follow.
- **No shadowing** — the real module stays in `sys.modules` with all its
attributes intact; every importer of that module (kimi_k3 DSpark
included) gets the genuine module.
- **Uses upstream's own degradation path** — vLLM's real module already
handles a missing flashinfer inside try/except (optional symbols degrade
to `None`, `_can_use_flashinfer` returns `(False, 0)`), so Ascend
naturally lands on the plain all-reduce + RMSNorm fallback instead of
downstream faking that state.

## Test plan

- [x] `py_compile` on the modified file.
- [x] On Ascend container: the real module
`vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm` imports OK
and its optional flashinfer symbols degrade to `None` (no import errors
on the kimi_k3 DSpark chain).
- [x] End-to-end `vllm serve` on A3 (B097): MiniMax-M3 with mooncake KV
pooling starts up, and `/v1/completions` (model `minimax-m3`) responds
correctly on both the P node and the D node.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8cc9aa5ad350f6f80cf3bebb298d410803ff75a9

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Main-branch counterpart of #18576, carrying the same two-file minimal
change.

In the int32 paged-cache scoring path, the final tile may contain pools
that are within configured capacity but beyond the query's actual
visible prefix. Key loads already use the visibility mask, while
block-table loads previously used only the capacity mask.

Use the existing `valid = (pools < max_pool_seq_len) & (pools <
visible)` mask for block-table loads as well. This is the only
production behavior change: invisible pool lanes no longer perform
page-table reads. Valid-input scores and selected token indices are
expected to remain unchanged.

The final diff contains only this mask change and boundary cases added
to the existing eager/graph regression test. No helper extraction,
wrapper reorganization, new benchmark/compilation-audit scripts or
documentation expansion is included.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API, serving flag, score formula or output-layout change. Dense score
allocation and `torch.topk` remain capacity-wide. This patch does not
resolve 1M-capacity scratch/TopK overhead, and no isolated end-to-end
speedup has been established for this mask-only change.

whitespace checks passed.

environment installation failed on this Windows host. Full CI remains

added.author: Deniz Özcan
added.subject: [BugFix][KV Pool] Prevent scheduler hang on lookup RPC failure (#18017)
added.body:
## What does this PR do / why do we need it?

Fixes #17923

Fix a failure mode in the AscendStore KV-pool lookup RPC path where an
exception in `LookupKeyServer` can terminate the request thread without
sending a REP response. The scheduler-side `LookupKeyClient` could then
block indefinitely in `recv()`, hanging the scheduler.

This change makes lookup failures degrade to a cache miss instead of an
unrecoverable scheduler stall.

### What changed?

- Poll the REP socket so the server thread can observe the shutdown
flag.
- Separate request receive failures from lookup-handler failures. If
receiving fails, do not attempt a REP send in an invalid ZeroMQ state;
exit the server loop and clean up from the socket-owning thread.
- Catch lookup-handler exceptions and reply with `0` hit tokens so a
valid REQ/REP exchange stays synchronized.
- Set a 1-second receive timeout on the scheduler-side REQ socket and
invalidate failed clients so the next lookup can build a fresh socket.
- Make client cleanup idempotent and terminate its private ZeroMQ
context.
- Wire client/server cleanup into the connector's `shutdown()` hook.
- Warn if an in-flight server handler has not exited after the bounded
1-second join; the owner thread closes its socket/context when it exits.
- Add regression tests for handler/receive errors, timeout behavior,
client reconstruction, idempotent cleanup, and connector shutdown.

A zero-hit response is wire-compatible with the existing protocol and is
handled as a normal cache miss by the scheduler.

Thread supervision/restart and forced cancellation of a blocked storage
handler remain out of scope; Python threads cannot be safely
force-cancelled.

Closes #17923

### Testing

- Fixed the CI-reported undefined `zmq` name and applied formatter
changes to the affected test and implementation files.
- Fixed mypy errors in the regression tests by importing typed ZeroMQ
symbols directly and annotating `server_holder`.
- Applied Ruff's requested import cleanup in both affected test files.
- Fixed a CPU unit-test fixture to mark its mocked lookup client as open
after the scheduler began checking the client's `closed` state.
- Latest commit: `c779332d72990a36e7aabff054ce6bdb5039c1a4` (DCO
sign-off included).
- CI for the latest commit is in progress; verify the CPU unit tests and
all required checks before merging.
- Focused unit tests and real NPU serving have not been run locally in
this environment. Ondre119 separately reported passing real-ZMQ
regression tests and 674 AscendStore CPU tests with 12 pre-existing
skips in their environment.

added.subject: [BugFix][CI] Fix cross-runner csrc L1 cache transport (#18123)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix cross-runner L1 snapshot reuse by giving every producer/consumer the
same workspace-relative transport path: `csrc/build_cache`.

The cache action's storage version includes the **literal path input**,
in addition to the logical key. Previously the CPU producer saved with
`/tmp/vllm-ascend-incremental-build-cache`, while consumers restored
with a runner-specific `runner.temp` path. Otherwise compatible logical
keys therefore searched different OBS namespaces. The archive also
records paths relative to `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, so a shared relative path
ensures extraction into the consumer's own workspace rather than the
producer's physical location.

Production evidence:
- [Producer
save](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/37869628129/job/113624720466)
- [Consumer miss with the same compatibility
prefix](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/37905719842/job/113746143445)

This patch:
- aligns all current L1 workflow callers on `csrc/build_cache`;
- preserves the helper-exported **absolute** build-time directory
instead of overriding it with the relative transport input;
- documents the transport-path contract and adds regression checks for
callers and nonfatal transport steps.

No cache-engine/CMake identity, schema (still 4), locks, L0, OBS
authorization, or ordinary-build fallback changes. Restore/save
transport errors remain nonfatal. This does not claim every unrelated
local filesystem/build error is nonfatal.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

subsequently compatible producer/consumer snapshots can be reused across

skipped**:

added.author: Wang Kunpeng
added.subject: [BugFix][Example] Pass int device_ids in offline_data_parallel.py to honor ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES (#18643)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #18638

vLLM's `EngineArgs._resolve_device_ids()` interprets the two entry types
differently:

- **str** entries → **physical device IDs** (the path intended for CUDA
UUID strings; the NPU/base `device_control_id_to_physical_device_id()`
is just `int(s)`)
- **int** entries (while the device-control env var is set) → **indices
into the visible set**

With `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7`, the string form therefore
resolved to physical cards `[0, 1, 2, 3]` instead of `[4, 5, 6, 7]`, and
worker init failed with:

```text
RuntimeError: Physical device 1 for logical device 1 is not visible in ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7
```

This was masked whenever `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` was unset or
contiguous from 0, because visible ordinals coincide with physical
device IDs there.

Change: pass ints (indices into the visible set) instead of strs. With
the fix, DP rank 0 resolves to physical cards 4, 5 and DP rank 1 to 6,
7; the example also keeps working when the env var is unset (ints
without the env var are already physical IDs).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No 

### How was this patch tested?

```bash
python vllm-ascend/examples/offline_data_parallel.py \
    --model="Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B" \
    --dp-size=2 \
    --tp-size=2 \
    --enable-expert-parallel
```

added.author: jack
added.subject: [BugFix] Request huge pages before Engram host registration (#18628)
added.body:
## Problem

When Engram CPU offload uses a large POSIX shared-memory scales mapping,
`aclrtHostRegisterV2` can fail before a 16-device TP1/DP16/EP service
starts:

```text
aclrtHostRegisterV2 failed: rc=207001 size=12288533824
```

The mapping is about 12.29 GB. The failure reproduced with the default
shmem THP policy and was avoided when the mapping was backed by shmem
transparent huge pages.

## Change

Request `MADV_HUGEPAGE` for each `SharedUvaBuffer` mapping immediately
after `mmap`/`SharedMemory` attachment and before `aclrtHostRegisterV2`.
A failure to issue the advisory is logged and registration continues,
preserving the existing fallback behavior.

The advisory is scoped to the Engram shared mapping; it does not change
the global THP policy or unrelated vLLM allocations. The implementation
uses Python's `mmap.madvise` API on the `SharedMemory` mapping.

## Validation

In the b097 D-side container with TP1 x DP16 x EP and
`gpu-memory-utilization=0.90`:

- 86/86 weight shards loaded.
- All 16 workers reached startup complete.
- All 16 API ports returned HTTP 200.
- A real Chat Completions request and concurrent requests to all 16
ports returned HTTP 200.
- No `aclrtHostRegisterV2` or OOM failures were present in the
successful startup log.
- The exact 12 GiB registration probe returned `rc=0` on all 16 devices
with shmem THPs.

The successful service run also required `HCCL_BUFFSIZE=3584` and
`HCCL_BUFFSIZE_EP=3584`; that independent EP communication-window issue
is outside this change.

## Checks

- `ruff check vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v41/engram/npu.py
tests/ut/models/test_engram.py`
- Direct Python probe confirmed `mmap.madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE)` succeeds
on a shared-memory mapping.
- The repository pytest harness could not start in this environment
because its `npu-smi` preflight executable was not runnable.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b

added.author: Zeyu Yang
added.subject: [CI][Misc] Skip interface break report instead of failing the NPU job (#18155)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The vLLM PR interface compatibility check reports an introduced
interface break as a pytest failure, which makes the whole Buildkite NPU
job fail. The break report is informational for PR authors, but a red
job makes it look like an environment or execution failure and blocks
the PR pipeline.

This PR changes the pytest entry to report an introduced break (analyzer
exit code 1) as a skipped case instead of a failure:

- The analysis result is still printed to the job log, so break details
remain fully visible and searchable.
- The case stays visible as SKIPPED in the test results, distinguishable
from a plain pass.
- The NPU job succeeds, so Buildkite reports green.

Analysis failures (non-zero exit code other than 1, e.g. missing Git
metadata or a crashed analyzer) still fail the test. The README in
tests/e2e/vllm_interface/ is updated to match the new behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This only affects the internal CI reporting behavior of the vLLM PR
interface compatibility check.

### How was this patch tested?

CI verification only (the test runs in vLLM's Ascend NPU Buildkite job
against a /workspace/vllm checkout). A PR that introduces an interface
break should now show the case as skipped and the job as successful; a
PR without an introduced break still passes as before.

added.subject: [Bugfix][KVPP] Support MultiConnector in KVPP validation (#18632)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

KVPP rejects a top-level `MultiConnector` even when its children are
supported `MooncakeConnectorV2` and `AscendStoreConnector`
configurations.

Normalize a direct connector into a one-entry list, or read the
configured children of a single-level `MultiConnector`. Validate every
entry against the two supported connector names and reject the V2
decode-consumer role. Reject empty connector lists. This keeps the check
flat and follows existing single-level connector checks in the
repository; no recursive helper or dict/object dual handling is
introduced.

Add regression tests for direct/combined configurations, connector
order, unsupported children, consumers and empty lists, plus a combined
configuration example. Nested MultiConnector wrappers remain
unsupported.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Supported KVPP connectors can be combined in a single-level
`MultiConnector`. Unsupported children remain rejected with their names
in the error.

### How was this patch tested?

- Both final branches: 6 TestKVPPConfig methods pass on the remote
Ascend runtime with their officially pinned vLLM sources. Executed via
unittest to avoid the container npu-smi/conftest startup issue; no test
assertions are skipped.
- Two Ascend A3 devices, DeepSeek-V2-Lite BF16, TP2, MRV1/eager;
inference matrix uses the v0.30.0 branch. Main has configuration-test
coverage.
- 270 short/mid outputs: 18 cases x 3 cache phases x 5 configurations
(plain, KVPP-only, default MultiConnector, async MultiConnector, direct
Store). Every configuration scores 17/18 per phase, with the same
baseline extract_code failure and no new expected-answer failures.
Includes 128-token cache boundaries through 1024 tokens.
- 48 long/batch outputs: 64/512/4096/8192-token single-occurrence facts,
batch 1 and mixed batch 4, cold/prefix/reset-reload. All expected
answers correct.
- The reference configuration disables KVPP and has no KV connector.
These runs compare configuration combinations; they are not an isolated
KVPP on/off comparison with identical MultiConnector settings. Full P/D
producer-consumer transfer has not been tested.
- All runtime and unit-test jobs exit 0; task container stopped. Tracked
Python hashes verified (1717 main Ascend, 1653 release Ascend, 2566 main
vLLM). Native runtime binaries reused, not rebuilt.
- Ruff lint/format and diff checks pass. Full format.sh ci was attempted
but pre-commit is unavailable locally.

The optional load_async line is omitted from the new combined-connector
example; default and explicit async modes were both tested.

added.author: leolee
added.subject: [Performance][DSA] Use activation exchange for PCP decode O projection (#18506)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Replace O-weight AllGather with activation exchange for sharded decode
in DeepSeek V4 and V4.1: token AllGather across PCP ranks, local O
projection, then ReduceScatter.

Share batch-scoped O projection handling, allocate graph-stable buffers
during initialization, and add unit coverage.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Optimizes sharded decode with PCP O projection weight sharding enabled.

### Decode performance

Three-round medians after warmup, measured on the same A3 node and 16
NPUs:

- MRV2, DP2 × TP1 × PCP8, EP, W4A8, INT8 Indexer, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`;
decode request sharding and PCP O-weight sharding enabled. MTP, Prefix
Cache, FlashComm, multistream and prefill/fused MC2 disabled.
- 32 input / 1024 output tokens, greedy decoding with `ignore_eos=true`;
concurrency 1 routes to DP0, concurrency 8 sends four requests to each
DP rank. `max_model_len=16384`, `max_num_seqs=96`,
`max_num_batched_tokens=512`, block size 128, 8 GiB KV cache per NPU,
`HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024`.
- Tested vLLM-Ascend `5c1a6aa3c` → `b503e9105`, with vLLM `ced6857afa`
and benchmark `19018e9cc`. The measured candidate contains the
activation-exchange optimization; this PR also includes buffer-capacity
hardening and test updates.

| Model | Concurrency | Decode token/s, before → after | Throughput gain
| TPOT ms, before → after | TPOT reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek V4 Flash | 1 | 18.296 → 28.010 | +53.09% | 54.673 → 35.717 |
34.67% |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash | 8 | 143.674 → 216.919 | +50.98% | 55.714 → 36.905
| 33.76% |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 1 | 20.028 → 32.749 | +63.52% | 49.951 → 30.551
| 38.84% |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 8 | 157.490 → 255.723 | +62.37% | 50.838 →
31.334 | 38.37% |

Decode throughput uses the common decode time window, excluding the
first and last 32 tokens of each request. All formal performance
requests succeeded with the required output length, no KV preemption,
and confirmed FULL graph replay.

Engram was disabled for both V4.1 runs. Both also used the same
compatibility fixes for SWA metadata and empty-rank FULL replay; those
fixes are outside this PR.

### Accuracy (DeepSeek V4 Flash)

GPQA Diamond first 100 frozen questions, repeated three times on one
service. Tested this PR at `67b8757f6`, with vLLM `8cc9aa5ad` and
benchmark `19018e9cc`.

- A3, 8 NPUs, MRV2, DP1 × TP1 × PCP8, EP, W4A8, INT8 Indexer,
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`; decode request and O-weight sharding enabled. MTP,
Prefix Cache, FlashComm, multistream and prefill/fused MC2 disabled.
- `max_model_len=65536`, `max_num_seqs=96`,
`max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, 16 GiB KV cache per NPU; CLI block size
128 (model-resolved block size 8). `HCCL_BUFFSIZE` and
`HCCL_BUFFSIZE_EP` both 1024.
- Non-streaming, concurrency 8, one worker, greedy decoding, seed 42,
thinking disabled, `ignore_eos=false`, maximum 8192 output tokens.
Identical prompts and option order across rounds; complete prompts
passed through a `{prompt}` template.

| Round | Correct | Accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 70/100 | 70% |
| 2 | 74/100 | 74% |
| 3 | 75/100 | 75% |

Mean: **73%**; range: **70%–75%**. All 300 requests succeeded with no
timeouts; prompt hashes and native evaluator results were verified. All
8 ranks completed graph capture, and FULL replay was confirmed during
each formal round.

Question 79 (zero-based) reached the output limit and yielded no
extractable answer in every round; it was counted as incorrect, keeping
the denominator at 100. Among the other 99 questions, 76 had the same
extracted answer in all three rounds and 23 varied.

Historical single-round scores were 79% and 71%; the current mean
differs by −6 and +2 percentage points. Those runs used another node, 16
NPUs with DP2, vLLM `ced6857afa`, and different sequence/batch/KV
budgets (16384/512/8 GiB). They are historical references, not a matched
before/after accuracy comparison.

### How was this patch tested?

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Nightly speculative-decoding acceptance checks need to support two
golden formats:

- A scalar checks position 0, preserving existing configs.
- A list checks its configured prefix of speculative positions.

Each checked position must be at least `baseline * (1 - tolerance)`.
Higher acceptance rates pass; the check only detects acceptance
regressions. Apply the shared validator to both single-node and
external-DP nightly tests. If a single-node config has no acceptance
baseline, skip that check instead of comparing against zero.

Per-position validation is based on
[jiajinzhu2/vllm-ascend#7](https://github.com/jiajinzhu2/vllm-ascend/pull/7),
