old_only.subject: [Revert] Revert "[BugFix][KV Cache] Propagate resolved prefix retention config" (#17480) (#18100)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Revert #17480 (`6f8c631cc4e3ef2f64853624883baf6fc73db620`) on
`releases/v0.30.0` to restore the previous dense checkpoint retention
behavior and mitigate a first-prefix-reuse regression with
Qwen3.5-397B-A17B + MTP.

#17480 made the resolved retention configuration effective in the Ascend
hybrid coordinator, AscendStore scheduler/worker, and GLM-Next cache
planner. With the option unset, the actual Ascend coordinator policy
changed from `None` (dense) to `0` (semantic checkpoints only). In the
A3 nightly workload, the first repeated long prompt then missed the
prefix cache and recomputed prefill. Reverting the PR restored that
first reuse and improved the measured nightly throughput.

This reverts the four product files and the associated
configuration-propagation tests/fixtures. The conflict in
`test_pool_worker.py` was resolved by keeping the later
`prefix_match_unit` fixture assignment while removing #17480's retention
assignment. The later GLM-5.3 store fixture also uses the parameterless
make_config() helper after the revert, matching #18029 and fixing the CI
mypy call-arg error. This provides a release mitigation while the
checkpoint behavior is investigated.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. The affected Ascend consumers return to their pre-#17480 behavior:
the legacy environment lookup resolves to `None` with the paired vLLM
v0.30.0, restoring dense retention and first-prefix reuse in the tested
workload. As a tradeoff, CLI/Python `prefix_cache_retention_interval`
overrides are again not propagated consistently through these Ascend
paths. No new option is introduced.

### How was this patch tested?

A3 NPU A/B validation used vLLM v0.30.0 (`ced6857afa`), Ascend release
baseline `ac1b7bceb`, and the exact four-file product-code reversal. The
product blobs in this revert commit were verified byte-for-byte against
the NPU-tested B arm. Both arms used identical compiled kernels and
serving parameters, with the same compatibility guard for an unrelated
optional DeepSeek V4.1 drafter import.

Configuration followed [the official A3 nightly
case](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/be0b61da22778b043eb2369b5f922b2a39ddc46d/tests/e2e/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-W8A8-mtp-A3.yaml):
single instance, TP16/DP1/EP, MRv2, MTP5 (draft eager),
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, prefix caching, Mamba `align`, 384-token cache/hash
pages, 16384 batch tokens, 133120 max model length, and 0.9 memory
utilization. CANN 9.2.0, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, AISBench
3.1.20260630. Seed 1024 was fixed for both arms.

Native AISBench used the first eight records of
`vllm-ascend/GSM8K-in131072-bs100-qwen3` (revision
`5f3da088f753ede3e4467d1ac3b3151798beba4d`): 131072 input tokens (131082
after the chat template), 1024 output tokens, concurrency 2, request
rate 0, streaming, temperature 0, and `ignore_eos=True`. The nightly
performance pass retained the native default of one warmup; formal
throughput covers eight requests, while counter snapshots include that
warmup.

| Measurement | With #17480 | Reverted |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Nightly output throughput | 71.101 token/s | 79.0071 token/s (+11.12%)
|
| Nightly mean TTFT | 13955.0 ms | 11130.4 ms |
| Nightly prefix-cache hit tokens, including warmup | 0 | 130944 |
| Fresh prompt's first repetition: cached tokens | 0 | 130944 |
| Fresh prompt's first repetition: TTFT | 8883.8 ms | 749.9 ms |

The fresh-prompt probe used the previously unused ninth dataset record
and ran `prime -> replay1 -> replay2`, one AISBench request per pass,
with no internal warmup. On the tested release, the with-PR arm
recovered 130944 cached tokens on `replay2`; it did not remain at zero
for all subsequent requests. Fully warmed eight-request replay reached
99.895% token hit rate in both arms, with output throughput 185.0027 vs
185.57 token/s. The regression is first reuse, rather than steady decode
throughput.

All 12 main passes completed: 40 formal requests plus two native
warmups, 42 successful requests, zero failures, and the expected
output-token counts. The +11.12% figure is an eight-request nightly
comparison, not a peak-throughput claim. Full nightly pytest and
accuracy evaluation were not run.

The current revert source also passed 222 targeted unit tests across
seven files on the A3 environment:

```text
tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py
tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_glm53_store.py
tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_scheduler.py
tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py
tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_cache_config.py
tests/ut/kv_transfer/test_ascend_store_layerwise_lifecycle.py
tests/ut/worker/test_glm5next_pooled_cache.py
```

Local validation: Python compilation, Ruff 0.14.0 checks and format
validation for all 10 changed Python files, and `git diff --check
upstream/releases/v0.30.0...HEAD` passed. Full `bash format.sh ci` was
attempted twice on Windows but could not complete: pre-commit's
Go-toolchain bootstrap for actionlint failed with `RemoteDisconnected`
before the complete hook run. Full repository lint/CI remains to be
verified by CI. For the GLM-5.3 fixture follow-up, the original runtime
TypeError was reproduced before the change; after the change all 222
scoped tests passed. The caller and helper also passed mypy 1.11.1 for
Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 with follow-imports=skip,
check-untyped-defs, and missing third-party imports ignored in the local
Windows environment.

old_only.author: lty
old_only.subject: [v0.30.0][Performance]narrow the KV save fence to requests with released blocks (#18094)
old_only.body:
## 1. Baseline and conclusion

- Baseline: the current save fence in `AscendStoreConnector`.
`handle_preemptions()` calls `KVPoolWorker.wait_for_previous_save()`,
which blocks the scheduler step until the **entire previous save batch**
has drained — i.e. every in-flight put of every request, whether or not
this step reuses any of those blocks.
- This PR narrows the fence to **exactly the requests whose blocks
become reusable this step** (`finished ∪ preempted`), carried through
the connector metadata as `released_req_ids`. Immediate block release is
kept unchanged.
- Measured on Atlas A2 (910B, CANN 9.1.0), Qwen3-32B W8A8, TP4,
single-engine `kv_both` with the mooncake backend:
- High prefix-hit, high-churn workload (16k input / 1-token output,
89.8% external hit): **+49%~52%** Input Token Throughput over the
whole-batch fence.
- No-hit workload (240 prompts, concurrency 60, ~3.5k input):
**+5.3%~5.4%** over the whole-batch fence, and **parity with
no-pooling** (±0.5%, within run-to-run noise) — the residual pooling
overhead in the no-hit case is eliminated.

## 2. Why the whole-batch fence is expensive

The fence exists to protect block reuse: KV blocks are freed immediately
when a request finishes or is preempted, so the in-flight puts reading
those blocks must complete before the scheduler can hand the blocks to a
new request.

The baseline enforces this by waiting for the **whole** previous save
batch on every step the hook fires. That waits for far more than reuse
requires:

- Requests that are still running keep their blocks — nobody can
overwrite them this step, yet the baseline waits for their puts too.
- On workloads with short outputs and high request turnover, many
requests finish every step, the fence fires effectively every step, and
the engine step gets serialized behind the full drain of in-flight RDMA
puts.
- The cost scales with in-flight put volume per step, which matches the
two measured extremes: a long-prompt no-hit workload (few save
completions per step) loses ~4.7% vs no-pooling, while the high-churn
hit workload gives up about a third of the achievable throughput (fence
29488 vs this patch 44400 avg, −33.6%).

## 3. Design

### 3.1 Carry `released_req_ids` in the connector metadata

- `metadata.py` — `AscendConnectorMetadata` gains `released_req_ids:
set[str]`, initialized from `preempted_req_ids`.
- `pool_scheduler.py` — when building the metadata it is set to
`set(scheduler_output.preempted_req_ids) |
set(scheduler_output.finished_req_ids)`.

### 3.2 Fence only those requests on the worker

- `ascend_store_connector.py` — `handle_preemptions()` now calls
`connector_worker.handle_released_saves(meta.released_req_ids)` instead
of `wait_for_previous_save()`.
- `pool_worker.py` — `handle_released_saves()` forwards to the sending
thread's `wait_for_requests_saved()`; the layerwise path is untouched
(its saves are already synchronized at each step's final layer).
- `kv_transfer.py` —
`KVCacheStoreSendingThread.wait_for_requests_saved()` polls
`stored_requests` (1 ms interval) until none of the given request ids
have a queued save chunk left:

```python
def wait_for_requests_saved(self, req_ids: set[str] | None) -> None:
    if not req_ids:
        return
    pending = set(req_ids)
    while True:
        self.raise_if_failed()
        with self.done_task_lock:
            pending &= self.stored_requests.keys()
            if not pending:
                break
        time.sleep(SAVE_REQUEST_POLL_INTERVAL_S)
```

The common case — no request released this step — costs one empty-set
return.

### 3.3 Why draining once is safe

1. A request queues no new save chunks after it finishes or is
preempted.
2. Its terminal state is flushed into exactly one `SchedulerOutput`, so
it appears in `released_req_ids` exactly once.
3. When the fence observes the request has no queued chunks left, every
put it will ever issue has completed — its blocks are safe to reallocate
from then on. No later fence needs to consider it again.
4. Preempted requests are covered by the same set (`preempted_req_ids`
is part of the union), and re-computation re-queues saves under the
still-alive request id, which a later release will fence again.

## 4. Test environment

- Single Atlas A2 server, 8× Ascend 910B, CANN 9.1.0; two containers
from the same image (host network, shared `/data`) used for
cross-checks.
- Server: Qwen3-32B W8A8 (`--quantization ascend`),
`--tensor-parallel-size 4` on NPU 0-3, `--block-size 128`,
`--max-model-len 40960`, `AscendStoreConnector` with `kv_role=kv_both`,
mooncake backend, `HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE=1`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=1`.
- Store: fresh `mooncake_master` per leg
(`--eviction_high_watermark_ratio 0.9 --eviction_ratio 0.15 --port
50088`) with a 20 GB segment config, so every leg starts from an empty
pool.
- Benchmark: ais_bench; metric is **Input Token Throughput** as reported
by the tool.
- Fairness: within each matrix all legs ran on the same machine state,
same image, fresh master; request success counts and external hit rates
are identical across legs, so the deltas are engine-side only.

## 5. Results

### 5.1 High prefix-hit, high-churn workload

`python3 aisbench_test.py --input_len 16384 --output_len 1 --data_num
160 --concurrency 32 --request_rate 0 --dataset_type prefix_cache
--repeat_rate 90% --prefix_num 16 --prefix_test`

16 distinct 16k prefixes, 90% repeat rate → external (pool) hit 89.80%
on **all** legs; local HBM prefix hit 0%; 160/160 requests succeeded on
all legs.

| Build | Input Token Throughput | Duration | Success |
|---|---|---|---|
| fence baseline (whole batch) | 29488.41 | 88.9 s | 160/160 |
| this patch, run 1| 44880.02 | 58.4 s | 160/160 |
| this patch, run 2 | 43920.74 | 59.7 s | 160/160 |

**+49.0% ~ +52.2% vs the fence baseline.** The two patched runs differ
by 2.2%, i.e. single-run noise on this ~60 s workload is ±1-2%; both
runs sit far above the baseline.

### 5.2 No-hit workload vs fence baseline and vs no-pooling

gsm8k 0-shot prompts (mean input ≈ 3500 tokens, no cross-request prefix
sharing → external hit ≈ 0), 240 prompts, concurrency 60.

| Build | Input Token Throughput | TTFT (mean) | ITL (mean) | vs fence |
vs no-pool |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fence baseline (whole batch) | 2157.02 | 7.34 s | 59.9 ms | — | −4.7%
|

| no-pooling, run 1 | 2262.41 | 6.15 s | 57.7 ms | +4.9% | — |

old_only.author: Ye Chenglin
old_only.subject: [BugFix][Attention] Respect per-layer KV cache dtype (#18062)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, MiniMax-M3 on Ascend A5 uses the mixed-KV
policy introduced in #17389: GQA layers are added to
`kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` and retain BF16 KV, while sparse layers use
FP8. Upstream `Attention` resolves the skip-layer override and passes
the effective per-layer dtype to the backend.

`AscendAttentionBackendImpl` currently ignores that argument and reads
the global cache dtype again. As a result, a BF16 GQA layer is treated
as FP8 and startup fails with:

```text
ValueError: The current GQA-related models adopt static quantization.
KV quantization is configured via "--kv-cache-dtype" upon service startup
```

Use the constructor's `kv_cache_dtype` argument when resolving the
backend dtype. Keep the existing static-quantization validation. This
completes the backend handling needed by the mixed-KV policy; the
global-dtype read already existed before #17389.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Layers with a KV dtype override now use their effective per-layer dtype.
No CLI or configuration change is introduced. Quantized layers without
the required static quantized weights still raise an error.

### How was this patch tested?

- The new layer-override regression test fails with the original GQA
ValueError before the fix.
- After applying this fix to the installed backend, `python -m pytest -q
tests/ut/attention/test_attention_v1.py` passes: **40 passed**. The
added tests cover global FP8 with layer auto/BF16, with and without the
recipe C8 flag, and preserve rejection of a genuinely quantized layer
lacking quantized weights.
- `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `codespell`, forbidden-import and
boolean-context-manager hooks, and `git diff --check` pass for the
changed files.
- Full `format.sh ci` did not complete because pre-commit's Go
environment download for actionlint failed with `zipfile.BadZipFile`;
this is not reported as a full CI pass.
- On two Ascend 950DT hosts (vLLM `0.30.0+empty`, vllm-ascend
`0.19.1rc2.dev2602+geee24e2e6.d20261007`, PyTorch `2.10.0`, torch-npu
`2.10.0.post7`), Prefill and Decode startup with DP2/TP4, MXFP8 model
weights, FP8 KV and EAGLE3 BF16 KV both pass the original GQA
initialization failure after this fix.
- **End-to-end PD validation completed with this fix plus the
independent block-alignment fix in #18014.** After the HCCL environment
repair, #18014 resolves the separate M3 Indexer metadata assertion
during graph capture. Both D ranks complete 81 FULL graphs; all four P/D
APIs are healthy. Fifteen PD requests pass, including four-way
concurrency, repeated 7742-token inputs and 299-token outputs. Both D
ranks record external KV transfer; zero preemptions or request errors.
This is startup/inference smoke coverage, not a performance or
model-accuracy benchmark.

The GQA patch is identical to #18003. The release graph/block-alignment
fix is kept exclusively in #18063 (backport of #18014); deploy both
release fixes for the reproduced mixed-KV setup.

### v0.30.0 backport

Backport of #18003 to `releases/v0.30.0` (base
`ac1b7bceb370265e8f794f38d32a88041b0c51c9`). Clean cherry-pick of
`f06e41b8d20f3ba24c60c2a7dfe8b6ad2b727d4d`; stable patch ID matches the
main PR exactly. This PR contains only the GQA dtype fix and its tests.

Backport validation on October 9:
- Re-ran the release test file against the installed patched backend:
**40 passed**. Verified the changed dtype assignment is identical using
AST comparison. Loading the entire release attention module into the
older serving image is blocked by an unrelated missing PCP helper
(`get_pcp_num_replicated_tokens`); this is not a full release-checkout
integration test.
- Ruff check/format, codespell, typos, forbidden-import and
boolean-context-manager hooks pass for the changed files; `git diff
--check` passes.
- Full local lint is not claimed: `format.sh ci` stalled installing
actionlint's Go environment; other broad local hooks encounter Windows
bash/Python executable limitations. The new PR's CI remains required.
- The two-host graph/inference results above are the previous
stacked-fix hardware validation, not a new run of the complete release
branch. Serving code/processes were not changed for the backport.

This is a cherry-pick of PR #18037 onto the 0.30.0 branch.

Share DSV4 transform tensors and cache KV plans, fuse scale correction
and cache
packing, and align DSpark context KV rotation and compressed attention
metadata. Restore the historical DSV4
Hadamard sequence while preserving the SFA baseline path and standard
CANN operator integration.

Add regression coverage for transform compatibility, cache planning,
context rotation, and NPU finalize behavior.

What this PR does / why we need it?
Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
How was this patch tested?
• ### What this PR does / why we need it?

Optimize the DeepSeek V4 TurboQuant path to reduce repeated allocations
and kernel launches, and keep DSpark
attention inputs consistent.

• Share read-only transform tensors, centroids, and norm lookup tables
across DSV4 layers; cache contiguous inverse
transforms and TQ KV execution plans.

• Fuse norm reduction, scale correction, and compact KV cache packing
into one Triton kernel.
• Rotate DSpark context KV into the same basis as queries and prevent
compressed TQ layers from using SWA-only
drafting metadata.

• Restore the historical DSV4 Hadamard sign sequence for compatibility
with the previously validated
implementation.

• Preserve the SFA baseline path and standard CANN TorchAPI/ACLNN
integration.

Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
No new configuration options or public API changes.

DSV4 TurboQuant uses the historical rotation sequence and corrected
DSpark context handling, which may change
generated outputs compared with the current baseline. Non-TQ paths,
including C8 and A5 quantization modes 1/2,
retain their existing logic.

How was this patch tested?
• 189 related unit tests passed, covering TurboQuant, DSA attention, and
DSpark context handling.
• 8 NPU finalize regression tests passed, covering packed codes, scale
correction, empty inputs, graph replay, and
compilation reuse across row counts.

• On NPU, compared against the historical implementation using the same
TurboQuant operator: transforms, centroids,
norm lookup tables, and forward/inverse/compression results matched
exactly for 1, 17, and 257 rows.

• Service smoke tests passed for short prompts, multi-turn chat,
streaming, and two concurrent requests before the
final Hadamard compatibility change.

• Applicable pre-commit checks passed. actionlint was skipped due to an
environment bootstrap issue; no workflow
files changed.

Long-context validation with the installed CANN 9.2 operator package
exposed numerical failures; the same
independent attention cases passed with the previously validated OPP
binaries. No framework workaround was
introduced. Full service validation after the final Hadamard change and
A5 hardware validation remain pending.

old_only.author: Ye Chenglin
old_only.subject: [BugFix][Attention][v0.30.0] Use a 64-token kernel minimum for M3 FP8 KV (#18132)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Clean backport of #18125 to `releases/v0.30.0`, cherry-picked with `-x`
from `e112a527e075225b0e8225bd7aa4cfd908bdeecb`. The stable patch-id is
identical (`89f9ae25231deee26e176ea575d85a8479d9e201`); no
release-specific code changes were needed. The branch is rebased on
`d3cc081829680ac79d491a282d7000db24c455db`, which already includes the
per-layer dtype fix #18062. The old skip-alignment alternative is
#18063; do not stack it with this PR.

MiniMax M3 with FP8 KV on hardware supporting FP8 attention retains BF16
KV in its GQA layers. The Ascend dense attention backend currently
advertises only a 128-token kernel block. Upstream heterogeneous-KV
alignment therefore expands the primary FP8 block to 256 tokens, which
is incompatible with the M3 indexer's 128-token block and causes
graph-capture initialization to fail.

For M3 FP8/FP8_E4M3 configurations with skip-quantization layers,
advertise dense kernel blocks `[64, 128]`. The existing upstream
alignment can then select 128 as the final cache block while keeping 128
available as the common kernel size with M3 sparse/indexer backends.
Gate this on `HardwareCapability.FP8_ATTENTION`; other models, non-FP8
configurations, configurations without skip layers, and calls outside an
engine context keep `[128]`.

Keep the initial cache block at 128. Setting `cache_config.block_size =
64` early in `utils.refresh_block_size` is insufficient on its own, and
doing so together with the backend change leaves the runner's
pre-model-load block table at 64 after alignment updates the cache
configuration to 128. In the reproduced single-group setup the existing
input-batch reinitialization check does not detect that transition. This
patch avoids that transition and requires no runner change.

This retains upstream alignment and is the release-branch alternative to
#18063 (main counterpart #18014). Its diff contains neither the platform
override nor the per-layer dtype fix; the latter is already present in
the release base through #18062 (main counterpart #18003).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The affected M3 mixed-KV configuration can initialize and run with the
supported 128-token cache/kernel block. No new CLI flag or environment
variable is introduced. The value 64 is a backend minimum used by
alignment, not the final block size of every layer. This PR does not
claim a measured KV-memory saving.

### How was this patch tested?

For this backport, verified identical patch-id, exact changed function
ASTs against the validated serving runtime, DCO, and reran the
backported configuration tests plus the existing attention tests: **56
passed**. No installed serving source was modified or service restarted
for this backport. The NPU/operator and serving results below are the
existing validation of the identical patch from #18125, not a new full
release-branch deployment.

- Added 16 configuration regression cases covering both M3
architectures, both FP8 strings, explicit/default block settings,
repeated upstream alignment, other models/dtypes/hardware, absent engine
context, absent skip layers, and preservation of a separate draft
model's shared cache configuration.
- Ran the new cases and the existing attention tests against the patched
serving-image modules: **56 passed**. Restoring the original `[128]`
backend declaration in an isolated process causes all eight mixed-KV
alignment cases to fail with `256 != 128`. These are configuration
tests, not full model loading.
- On Ascend 950DT, ran eight small BF16 paged-GQA operator checks with
64/128-token pages, noncontiguous block tables, KV lengths
65/129/257/1025 and query lengths 1/4/16. All pass against an FP32
reference (`atol=0.01`, `rtol=0.02`); maximum observed absolute error
was 0.002543.
- Single-host, eight-device **DP2/TP4** serving with MiniMax-M3 MXFP8
weights, FP8 KV, EAGLE3 BF16 KV/spec3, max model length 133000, max
sequences 256 and FULL_DECODE_ONLY/max graph capture 1024. #18003 was
retained and #18014 removed. Both DP ranks complete **81 FULL graphs**
and both APIs become healthy. **14/14** inference requests pass,
including concurrent requests, four 7741-token inputs with prefix reuse,
and four exact 1-to-100 outputs of 299 tokens.
- Runtime cache inspection confirms the runner's initial block, actual
block-table dimensions, cache specs and selected common kernel block are
all 128. GQA, sparse, indexer and draft caches retain their actual
per-layer byte strides. Temporary cache-audit instrumentation was
removed from installed source after validation; it is not included in
this PR.
- Serving validation used vLLM `0.30.0+empty`, vllm-ascend
`0.19.1rc2.dev2602+geee24e2e6.d20261007`, PyTorch `2.10.0` and torch-npu
`2.10.0.post7`, with the changed functions applied to that image. The
production function ASTs were checked against this PR. This is not a
full integration run of the current main checkout, a performance
benchmark, a full accuracy evaluation or a maximum-context test.
Two-host PD was not rerun because the second host was unavailable; the
single-host test omits KV-transfer configuration.
- Backport changed-file Ruff check/format, forbidden-import checks,
boolean-context checks and `git diff --check` pass. Full local
`format.sh ci` again stalled while installing actionlint's Go
environment and was stopped after 90 seconds; a full local lint/CI pass
is not claimed.

old_only.subject: [Feature][P/D][v0.30.0] Support Mooncake V2 KV receive failure handling (#18147)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport of #18146 to `releases/v0.30.0` (cherry-picked without
conflicts).

Support request-level KV receive failure reporting in
`MooncakeConnectorV2` through vLLM's `KVConnectorTransferResults`,
including hybrid caches with multiple KV groups. Drain receive
completion and failure together, attribute transfer errors to the
affected requests, and retain producer release notifications after
worker completion is aggregated. Log failed request IDs and the
configured failure policy on D.

Preserve externally supplied request IDs in the PD proxy, with
`X-Request-Id` taking precedence over the JSON body. Update existing
connector tests for the new completion results.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Multi-group KV transfer failures follow `kv_load_failure_policy`
instead of being ignored. When this option is omitted, vLLM defaults to
`fail`, so failed KV transfers are handled as request failures without
any additional configuration. Clients can supply a request ID through
the proxy and correlate it with failure logs.

### How was this patch tested?

The functional experiment results below are from the original
main-branch validation; the experiment was not rerun on the release
branch.

Ascend A5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `MooncakeConnectorV2`, P/D DP4 TP1,
six KV groups, and `kv_load_failure_policy=fail`. Injected receive
failures based on externally supplied request IDs, using both header and
body IDs; the randomized phase used concurrency 4.

| Requests | HTTP 200 | HTTP 500 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deterministic and recovery checks | 8 | 3 |
| Randomized injection | 53 | 47 |
| Total | 61 | 50 |

All 111 requests matched the expected outcome. All 50 failed requests
reached `FINISHED_ERROR`; P-side release and D-side cleanup were
verified. Running/waiting requests and KV-cache usage returned to zero
on all P/D ranks. Temporary fault-injection code is excluded from this
PR.

These runs cover simulated receive failures, not actual network faults
or same-request cross-TP failure aggregation.

old_only.subject: [releases/v0.30.0][SpecDecode][BugFix] Disable EPLB for PCP-only replicated drafts (#18194)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport #17959 to `releases/v0.30.0`. This author-submitted PR replaces
the bot-created backport #18188.

With MRV2 MTP, a target configured with TP=1, DP=1, PCP>1 and EPLB
enabled creates a replicated draft that executes with PCP=1. Inheriting
target EPLB causes draft configuration reconstruction to fail with `EPLB
requires tensor, prefill-context, or data parallelism, but got TP=1,
PCP=1, DP=1`.

Disable EPLB and clear redundant experts for this replicated draft
configuration in the existing PCP helper. Copy declared `EPLBConfig`
fields with `dataclasses.replace` so the target's transient
communicator-selection marker is not copied. Preserve draft EP and
target EPLB, and skip draft registration with the target EPLB state when
the draft's own EPLB is disabled. Preserve the release branch's Engram
configuration handling so a PCP=1, DP=1 draft also disables Engram
shared memory without changing the target configuration.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. TP=1, DP=1, PCP>1 MRV2 replicated drafts automatically disable EPLB
and emit a warning, allowing configuration initialization to continue.
The draft uses a fixed expert layout while the target continues load
balancing. Draft configurations with TP>1 or DP>1 retain their existing
EPLB behavior. No new configuration options are introduced.

### How was this patch tested?

- On commit `004de43a4dad7ee1a65e3b9590a5b55478cabcac`, ran the two
affected unit test files in the existing Ascend container using the
repository's CPU mock mode and the exact paired vLLM commit
`ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607`: **80 passed**. Both the
release tag and the verified-main pin resolve to this vLLM commit. Used
separate source snapshots on `PYTHONPATH` to preserve the container's
installed checkouts. No dependency installation or native rebuild was
performed.

To select the same mock mode on an NPU host, `tests/ut/conftest.py` must
see a failing `npu-smi` probe. The following uses a private stub for
this pytest process; run from the candidate Ascend checkout with the
paired vLLM source first on `PYTHONPATH`:

```bash
mock_bin="$(mktemp -d)"
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n' > "$mock_bin/npu-smi"
chmod +x "$mock_bin/npu-smi"
PATH="$mock_bin:$PATH" TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 python -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/worker/test_mtp_pcp_speculator_v2.py \
  tests/ut/worker/v2/test_eplb_controller.py
```

- The topology test uses real `EPLBConfig` objects and explicit draft
EPLB expectations. It checks that the PCP>1, TP=1, DP=1 Engram case
disables draft EPLB while preserving target EPLB and Engram settings,
and that DP>1 cases retain draft EPLB. Existing coverage checks
redundant-expert clearing, target configuration isolation, inherited
draft-loader reconstruction, and draft registration while preserving
target registration and its async EPLB loop.
- Negative control: restored only `pcp_utils.py` from the release base,
retaining its Engram handling, and ran
`test_draft_runtime_config_preserves_target_worker_topology[2-1-1-True-False]`.
It failed as expected because draft EPLB remained enabled (`True`
instead of `False`). Restored the candidate helper before the full
passing run.
- Ruff lint and format checks, Python AST parsing, and `git diff
--check` passed for the affected files. The rebased branch merges
cleanly with the current release base.
- CI for the updated commit is pending. NPU startup/inference, accuracy,
and performance have not been validated for this backport.

old_only.author: muziyuhui666
old_only.subject: [BugFix][MoE] Fix E8M0 scale dtype for CANN MegaMoE (#18216)
old_only.body:
Cherry-picked from #18157 for releases/v0.30.0.
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes the E8M0 weight scale dtype passed to CANN MegaMoE by the
W8A8-MXFP8 and W4A4-MXFP4 fused MoE implementations.

The E8M0 weight scales are stored in checkpoints as `uint8` tensors.
When preparing the per-expert scale lists for CANN MegaMoE, the existing
implementation only clones these tensors, leaving their dtype as
`torch.uint8`.

However, `npu_mega_moe` requires `l1_weights_sf` and `l2_weights_sf` to
use the semantic dtype `torch.float8_e8m0fnu`. As a result, models using
these quantization schemes fail during the profiling run with an error
similar to:

`RuntimeError: l1_weights_sf[0] dtype must be float8_e8m0fnu, but got
Byte.`

This PR:

- Reinterprets the cloned W8A8-MXFP8 MegaMoE weight scales as
`torch.float8_e8m0fnu`.
- Reinterprets the cloned W4A4-MXFP4 MegaMoE weight scales as
`torch.float8_e8m0fnu`.
- Applies the fix to both the `w13`/L1 and `w2`/L2 scale lists.
- Preserves the original E8M0 bit patterns by using
`view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu)` instead of performing a numeric dtype
conversion.
- Adds unit tests covering the resulting dtype and bit-pattern
preservation.

The change is limited to the CANN MegaMoE weight preparation paths for
these two quantization schemes.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

Models using CANN MegaMoE with W8A8-MXFP8 or W4A4-MXFP4 quantization can
now initialize and execute without failing because the weight scale
tensors are reported as `Byte`.

This does not introduce any API or configuration changes.

### How was this patch tested?

Added or updated unit tests in:

- `tests/ut/quantization/methods/w8a8/test_w8a8_mxfp8.py`
- `tests/ut/quantization/methods/w4a4/test_w4a4_mxfp4.py`

The tests verify that:

- The generated `w13` and `w2` MegaMoE scale lists use
`torch.float8_e8m0fnu`.
- Reinterpreting the scales preserves their original E8M0 bit patterns.
- Both W8A8-MXFP8 and W4A4-MXFP4 paths are covered.

The targeted MegaMoE unit tests passed:

`2 passed`

Python syntax compilation checks also passed for both modified
implementation files.

old_only.author: muziyuhui666
old_only.subject: [BugFix][MoE] Handle missing MegaMoE activation kwargs (#18218)
old_only.body:
Cherry-picked from #18137 for releases/v0.30.0.
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR prevents the CANN MegaMoE path from raising a `TypeError` when
the routed layer's `mega_moe_activation_kwargs` is `None`.

`FusedMC2CommImpl._apply_cann_mega_moe()` currently expands the layer
attribute directly:

```python
**layer.mega_moe_activation_kwargs
```

However, this attribute may be `None` when the per-layer MegaMoE
activation metadata is unavailable. Expanding it as keyword arguments
results in the following exception:

```text
TypeError: argument after ** must be a mapping, not NoneType
```

This change resolves the MegaMoE activation arguments in the following
order:

1. Use the activation arguments bound to the current routed layer.
2. Fall back to the activation arguments resolved by the shared
communicator.
3. Use an empty mapping if neither source provides activation arguments.

The layer-specific arguments remain preferred. This preserves the
correct activation parameters for models and layers that provide them,
while preventing MegaMoE inference from crashing when the layer metadata
is missing.

`layer.mega_moe_activation_kwargs` is `None` and to verify that the

### What this PR does / why we need it?

release-specific code changes and includes the original regression
tests.

Hybrid PD decode requests with `recompute_scheduler_enable=true` start
from transferred state at `N-1` prompt tokens. The existing MRV1 guard
rejects their decode graph even when the scheduled query has the uniform

consumer with recompute enabled, using the helper already present on the

query-width checks, ordinary hybrid prefill protection, and DCP guard.
Input preparation and prefill flags are unchanged.

existing decode graph, reducing first-token latency. No new

old_only.author: ZixuanWang
old_only.subject: [BugFix][Worker] Zero static KV buffers after cudagraph capture (v0.30.0 backport) (#18263)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport of #17659 to releases/v0.30.0.

GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA+SFA hybrid, fp8 C8 KV cache) collapses into emitting
'!' forever on A5 with FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture. During capture the
dummy forward bypasses the block allocator: SFA writes carry
slot_mapping=-1 (dropped by the scatter op), while KDA state_indices
default to slot 0 and really execute, writing bf16 dummy state into slot
0 of the backing shared with the SFA fp8 pool; reinterpreted as fp8 e4m3
those bytes contain NaN encodings. Nothing resets the buffers after
capture, so the first real request reads resident NaNs that defeat the
softmax additive mask and poison the residual stream.

This PR zeroes every persistent KV/state tensor registered in
static_forward_context once, right after capture_model().

Note: this intentionally carries the ORIGINAL implementation of #17659
(RuntimeError fallback chain), not the revised dtype-dispatch + chunked
version now on main, so we can compare v0.30.0 CI behaviour against
main's (where the original fallback's same-size temporary OOMed a2
runners). Happy to sync to the final main version before merge - see
#17659 for the full discussion.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Startup-only internal fix.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests added: tests/ut/worker/test_zero_static_kv_buffers.py
(original version from #17659)
- Manually verified on A5 with GLM-5.3-Flash: without this fix the model
emits '!' after FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture; with it, output is normal.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607

old_only.author: XuChi
old_only.subject: [BugFix][Model] Point users at the recipe fix when oproj capacity is exceeded (#18272)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Companion to #18126 (against `main`), cherry-picked to the
`releases/v0.30.0` branch where users actually run this code.

Improves the `ValueError` raised in `dsa_v1.py::_forward_o_proj` when
the fine-grained oproj TP static exchange capacity cannot cover the
local token count. The old message only echoed two numbers:

```
ValueError: oproj static exchange capacity must cover local tokens, got 16 and 240.
```

Real user case: DeepSeek-V4-Flash + PD disaggregation (decode dp16×tp1)
with `--max-num-batched-tokens 240 --max-num-seqs 4`, speculative
decoding (dql=4), and `finegrained_tp_config
{"oproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8}` crashed at startup with the message
above. The capacity is `max(largest capture bucket,
min(max_num_batched_tokens, max_num_seqs * decode_query_len))` = 16
while the profiling/warmup dummy batch equals `max_num_batched_tokens` =
240, so the raise fired — but users could not tell (a) that this is a
fine-grained-TP recipe constraint rather than an engine bug, or (b) how
to fix the config.

The new message states the constraint (`capacity >=
max_num_batched_tokens`) and both fixes — set `--max-num-batched-tokens`
to `max_num_seqs * decode_query_len`, or raise the largest entry of
`cudagraph_capture_sizes` — with the user's `max_num_seqs` inlined.
Rendered at the user's numbers:

```
oproj static exchange capacity (16) must cover local tokens (240). Fine-grained oproj TP requires capacity >= max_num_batched_tokens. Please set --max-num-batched-tokens to max_num_seqs * decode_query_len (currently max_num_seqs=4), or raise the largest cudagraph_capture_sizes entry.
```

Message style follows the repo's existing compound-error precedent
(`profiling_chunk_config` in `ascend_config.py`: fact + numbers +
"Please set X, or Y"; the second fix names the actual config key,
matching the knob-naming style of the `potential_max_tokens` warning in
`utils.py`). `scheduler_config` is read from `self.vllm_config` — the
same object the capacity computation three lines above already uses —
inside the failure branch only, so there is zero hot-path cost.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Only the error message text, which becomes actionable. No behavior
change.

### How was this patch tested?

- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` pass locally, and the rendered
message was verified by local string simulation (pasted above).
- The existing UT `test_o_proj_capacity_covers_profile_and_decode`
asserted the old message text, so its `pytest.raises` match is updated
to the new core fragment and now also asserts the inlined numbers
(`capacity (N) must cover local tokens (M)`); its `scheduler_config`
mock gains the `max_num_seqs` attribute the raise path now reads. No
vllm/torch environment on this machine, so UT verification relies on CI;
the change is a single error-message edit and needs no NPU run.

old_only.author: weiguihua2
old_only.subject: [BugFix][v0.30.0][SFA] Preserve PCP decode ownership and KV-copy kernel reuse (#18266)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

When PCP shards decode token rows, the feature-sharded O-proj previously
all-reduced projections of different tokens at matching row offsets.
Gather decode rows before the local feature-sharded GEMM, then
reduce-scatter the summed projections to their owning PCP ranks.
Replicated decode keeps its existing all-reduce, and prefill keeps its
full-weight path.

Allocate the collective buffers in `AscendSFAPCPImpl.__init__`, using
activation dtype and the O-proj weight's actual device. Compatible
layers reuse the same four graph-stable AG/RS buffers through
`o_proj_full_pools`; buffer roles, devices, dtypes and shapes have
separate pool keys. Size them for the larger of the decode token budget
(`max_num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)`) and graph capture sizes,
including padded rows. This prepares buffer capacity for speculative
tokens without changing the existing gate that disables sharded decode
when speculative decoding is configured.

Also mark `slots` as `do_not_specialize` in the PCP KV-copy Triton
kernel so contiguous slot slices with different pointer alignments reuse
the same compilation. Preserve specialization of the inner strides
required by Ascend lowering.

pick-from: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18265

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes SFA PCP sharded-decode O-proj token ownership and avoids redundant
PCP KV-copy compilation for slot slices. No configuration or API
changes. The combinations of unsliced O-proj with sharded decode, and
sliced O-proj with replicated decode, retain their existing projection
behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

Validated the updated source files on an Ascend NPU container with the
installed vLLM 0.30.0 runtime:

- `pytest -q tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_cp.py`: **189 passed**.
Includes row ownership, quantized weights, TP reduction, activation
dtype, speculative-token capacity, graph padding, cross-layer buffer
sharing, dtype/capacity isolation, and weight-device isolation cases.
- `pytest -q
--confcutdir=tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton
tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_pcp_kv_cache.py`:
**34 passed on a real NPU**. Checks exact KV bytes and a single JIT
cache entry across slot offsets, lengths, dtypes, and C8/non-C8 layouts.
- Ruff, formatting, spelling, repository Python checks, actionlint and
staged gitleaks checks passed. Windows-incompatible hook entrypoints
were executed through native tools/Git Bash; all 114 shell scripts
across both target branches passed ShellCheck after CRLF normalization
in scratch files, without editing tracked scripts.

The O-proj unit tests mock distributed collectives; they do not
establish full-service MTP support or real multi-rank HCCL graph
performance.

old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport of #18241 to `releases/v0.30.0`.

GLM-5.3-Flash can reuse sparse selections while positions advance. In
the A5 target path, this can leave a predicted `ori_topk_length` of 2049
for only 2048 valid indices, even when the query shape is unchanged.

Count valid entries from the actual sparse indices on every SMLA call,
mask graph-padding rows to zero, and generate the plan from the same
lengths, query offsets, head dimensions, and physical indices width
passed to the operator. Retain persistent buffers for graph replay and
preserve the CP head-count override. Update the existing regression
coverage for target reuse, trimmed queries, draft execution, and
padding.

The backport applies cleanly and has the same stable patch ID as the
mainline change. It does not include Mooncake connector changes.

Refs #15665

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. The A5 GLM-5.3-Flash SMLA path uses lengths and plans consistent
with its actual selections, including reused top-k selections and
graph-padding rows.

### How was this patch tested?

`tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_nope_metadata.py` using the release
branch's production helpers, isolated from unavailable vLLM/NPU imports,
with real CPU PyTorch. All passed. External SMLA operators were stubbed;
this is not a real kernel or model run.
- Ran the target-reuse regression against the unpatched release base
`f8f1180e30fc485cb1f5ad0a1edf1795b5f17f5b`; it failed on the incorrect
lengths as expected and passes with the backport.
- Verified that the patch ID matches mainline commit
`a91d021b58d1b7bb6c0affcbd76e3d976cc1a7b7` and `git diff --check` is
clean.
- Local Ruff checks/formatting, changed-file spelling checks, and the
logger check passed. The full Linux pre-commit run and full CPU UT runs
will be checked in this PR's CI; some shell hooks cannot run in the

release backport.

old_only.author: Li Shuai
old_only.subject: [BugFix] Pin EC cache load device to correct NPU index in TP>1 (#18291)
old_only.body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes a prefill-worker crash (NPU AI Core errcode=95, MTE DDR address
out of range) on EC consumer nodes in disaggregated EPD deployments with
**tensor parallelism > 1**.

**Root cause**: upstream `ECExampleConnector.start_load_caches` only
appends the device index to the safetensors load device when
`current_platform.is_cuda_alike()` is True:

```python
device = current_platform.device_type          # "npu"
if current_platform.is_cuda_alike():           # False on Ascend NPU
    device = f"{device}:{current_platform.current_device()}"
```

`is_cuda_alike()` returns False on Ascend NPU, so the device string
stays a bare `"npu"`. Consequently, **every TP rank loads the EC
(encoder) cache onto the default device `npu:0`**, regardless of the
device it is actually bound to. With TP=2, rank 1 executes
`inputs_embeds[is_multimodal] = mm_embeds_flat` on its own device while
`mm_embeds_flat` still lives on `npu:0` — the cross-device MTE access
trips errcode=95 and crashes the worker. TP=1 masks the bug because the
single rank resides on `npu:0` anyway.

**Fix**: patch `start_load_caches` via the vllm-ascend platform patch
mechanism so the device index is also appended on Ascend NPU (`device ==
"npu"`), matching the behavior CUDA already has. The patch only takes
effect when the connector acts as an **EC consumer** (where the crash
occurs); EC producer nodes and non-EC deployments fall through to the
original upstream implementation unchanged.

An upstream vLLM fix is planned separately; this patch unblocks Ascend
users until it lands in a released vLLM version.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No. The patch is transparent to users:
- Non-EC deployments and EC producer nodes: behavior is byte-for-byte
identical to upstream.
- EC consumer nodes: the EC cache is now loaded onto each rank's bound
device instead of `npu:0`. No CLI flags, configs, or APIs change; the
previously-crashing TP>1 multimodal prefill scenario now succeeds, and
TP=1 behavior is unchanged.

## How was this patch tested?

- **Reproduction setup**: EPD disaggregated deployment on Ascend 950DT —
E node (TP=1, ec_producer), P node (TP=2, ec_consumer + kv_producer), D
node (TP=2, kv_consumer), model Qwen3.6-27B, multimodal (image) requests
over the EC path.
- **Before fix**: rank 1 of the P node crashes with `RuntimeError: NPU
function error: device error type 3, error code 507035, errcode=95` in
`_merge_multimodal_embeddings` (`inputs_embeds[is_multimodal] =
mm_embeds_flat`); located with debug probes +
`ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`.
- **After fix**: multimodal request completes end-to-end (first-token
latency ~1.3 s, full response 1888 chars, correct image analysis).
- **Regression check**: TP=1 EC path unchanged (loads land on `npu:0` as
before); non-EC paths unaffected (patch is a no-op for them).
---

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607

---------

old_only.subject: [BugFix][EPLB][v0.30.0] Preserve NPU format for expert buffers (#18232)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport of #18231 to `releases/v0.30.0`, based on the original
NPU-format allocation fix from #18015 by @hust17yixuan.

EPLB allocates receive buffers with `torch.empty_like` on
`EplbExpertTensorList`. On ACLNN-only devices, ordinary `empty_like` can
convert an internal NPU storage format to ND and leave the receive
buffer incompatible with its source expert tensor.

Use `torch_npu.empty_with_format` with each source tensor's format,
dtype, layout, and device. Preserve the storage-offset and stride
checks, and support ND integer tensors such as encoded quantization
scales without misclassifying them as NZ-only weights.

The tensor list supports the default EPLB allocation call;
tensor-property overrides are rejected. Non-NPU tensors use ordinary
`torch.empty_like` for CPU test coverage.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No public API change. EPLB receive buffers preserve the source expert
tensor's NPU storage format.

### How was this patch tested?

- CPU unit tests with a mocked NPU allocator: 24 passed across
`tests/ut/ops/test_routed_experts.py` and
`tests/ut/ops/test_eplb_v2_recording.py` on this branch. Coverage
includes ND/NZ format propagation, ND integer scales, property-override
rejection, nonzero storage offsets, and stride mismatches.
- `bash format.sh ci` and `git diff --check` passed.
- The full remote mypy gate could not start because fetching the pushed
source timed out.
- Real NPU smoke validation could not proceed because the available
runtime failed during device initialization; NPU allocation and
migration validation remain pending.

old_only.body:
Revert of PR #18263 (merged onto `releases/v0.30.0`).

Original PR: #18263
Original author: @Toneymiller
Merge commit: `334d4d70505836f1290404a311cfe2c9529ed06d`

---
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport of #17659 to releases/v0.30.0.

GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA+SFA hybrid, fp8 C8 KV cache) collapses into emitting
'!' forever on A5 with FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture. During capture the
dummy forward bypasses the block allocator: SFA writes carry
slot_mapping=-1 (dropped by the scatter op), while KDA state_indices
default to slot 0 and really execute, writing bf16 dummy state into slot
0 of the backing shared with the SFA fp8 pool; reinterpreted as fp8 e4m3
those bytes contain NaN encodings. Nothing resets the buffers after
capture, so the first real request reads resident NaNs that defeat the
softmax additive mask and poison the residual stream.

This PR zeroes every persistent KV/state tensor registered in
static_forward_context once, right after capture_model().

Note: this intentionally carries the ORIGINAL implementation of #17659
(RuntimeError fallback chain), not the revised dtype-dispatch + chunked
version now on main, so we can compare v0.30.0 CI behaviour against
main's (where the original fallback's same-size temporary OOMed a2
runners). Happy to sync to the final main version before merge - see
#17659 for the full discussion.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Startup-only internal fix.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests added: tests/ut/worker/test_zero_static_kv_buffers.py
(original version from #17659)
- Manually verified on A5 with GLM-5.3-Flash: without this fix the model
emits '!' after FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture; with it, output is normal.

old_only.subject: [Feature][Model][v0.30.0] Wire MiniMax-M3 into FlashComm sequence parallel MoE (#18324)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport #18292 to `releases/v0.30.0`.

MiniMax-M3 accepted the FlashComm configuration, but its model path did
not propagate sequence parallelism into the dense/attention path or the
MoE runner. Enabling `enable_flashcomm1` therefore selected the backend
without establishing the model-level SP layout.

This change follows the DeepSeek/GLM/Kimi native-SP pattern:

- enables sequence parallelism for both dense and MoE layers in
MiniMax-M3;
- constructs attention output projections with TP all-reduce disabled
and applies SP ReduceScatter;
- keeps residuals sequence-sharded across consecutive layers;
- wraps TP-sharded dense MLP weights with SP AllGather/ReduceScatter;
- propagates `is_sequence_parallel` into `FusedMoEFactory`;
- restores full-token tensors at PP transport, final output, and
requested EAGLE3 auxiliary-state boundaries;
- aligns ACL Graph bucket-sized hidden inputs to the actual positions
dimension before the first SP shard; and
- adds focused regression coverage.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. MiniMax-M3 deployments with FlashComm / sequence-parallel MoE
enabled now execute the model-level SP data flow across both dense and
MoE layers. Configurations without sequence-parallel MoE are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Both commits from #18292 cherry-picked onto `releases/v0.30.0` without
conflicts.
- `git range-diff` confirms both backport commits are patch-identical to
#18292.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Python `compileall` passed for all changed Python files.
- The original first commit was validated on A3:
`tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_minimax_m3.py` reported 10 passed.

Limitations:

- Ruff is not installed in the local backport environment; release CI
remains authoritative.
- A full MiniMax-M3 accuracy run and profiler confirmation remain
required before performance acceptance.

old_only.author: chenzhh69
old_only.subject: [Feature][KV Cache] Enable overlay backing for Step-3.5/3.7 multi-group attention models and exempt their budget scale (#18317)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
vLLM #51718 derives `num_blocks` from the largest KV cache group's
bytes-per-block, but Ascend runners keep contiguous per-layer buffers
for every group, so per-layer sizing totals `num_blocks * sum(all
groups' pages)` and exceeds device memory whenever more than one group
is non-trivial. `_scale_kv_cache_memory_for_multi_group` compensates by
shrinking the advertised budget by `bytes_per_block / sum_pages`.

Step-3.5/3.7 (`model_type` `step3p5`/`step3p7`) are multi-group
attention models (full + sliding-window attention): every group consumes
identical bytes per block, so the runner's shared-backing path
materializes one physical block per block id — exactly the #51718
overlay contract, no capacity loss. Hybrid attention/Mamba models
already take this path.

- `model_runner_v1.py`: extend the shared-backing allocation gate from
`hybrid_with_attn_and_mamba` to also cover Step-3.5/3.7 via
`self.is_step_model`, computed from
`model_config.hf_text_config.model_type`; the non-empty
`kv_cache_tensors` guard is preserved.

- `worker.py`: gate the budget exemption on `has_mamba or is_step_model`
instead of the shape-derived `uniform_group_pages`, so the planner keeps
the full budget the shared backing can consume for exactly the models
that use it. Other multi-group models keep the per-layer scale path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No.
### How was this patch tested?
CI test.

old_only.author: Haoxin Zong
old_only.subject: [Performance][Model][v0.30.0] Fuse MiniMax-M3 QK norm, RoPE and KV cache insertion (#18325)
old_only.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Backport of #18235 to `releases/v0.30.0`. All six commits were
cherry-picked without conflicts, and `git range-diff` confirms they are
patch-identical to the source PR.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MiniMax-M3's attention preparation launches separate normalization,
RoPE, and two cache-insertion operators. This change performs four Gemma
RMSNorms, partial NeoX RoPE, and main K/V plus index K cache writes in
one Triton kernel. Only Q and index Q are materialized. RoPE rows are
read directly inside the kernel, eliminating the external gather as
well.

Support both packed projections and separate QKV/index projections used
by W8A8 models, without adding a concat/copy. Vectorize Q/K and index
Q/K over contiguous head rows within one program per token. A tested
two-program-group variant was slower at 192 tokens (18.23 us versus
14.40 us), so this version introduces no additional streams or
synchronization kernels.

Based on main `05fa3be5f`; independent of #15772. References: #15772 and
vLLM's
[`fusedMiniMaxQNormRopeKVInsertKernel`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7566d83bd35cdfd7cd3f9e521a005d2fc1ed1c33/csrc/libtorch_stable/fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu).

Preserve independent main/index slot mappings, negative slots, graph
padding, cache strides, and BF16 normalization rounding. Cache capacity
(`num_blocks`) is dynamic and is not a kernel compilation parameter.
Cache writes, indexer and sparse attention remain inside an opaque
attention boundary, with no duplicate insertion calls.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Automatically enable for BF16 NPU input, matching 128-wide main/index
heads, NeoX RoPE, matching norm epsilon and at most 512 tokens including
padding. Both packed and separate index projections are supported. Other
configurations retain the existing path. No new flags or environment
variables.

### How was this patch tested?

A3 operator tests on host 197: CANN 9.2.0, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu
2.10.0.post4, triton 3.5.0 / triton_ascend 3.2.2. BF16, Q/KV/index heads
8/1/1, head dimension 128, rotary dimension 64, block size 128, 5392
blocks, separate index projection.

The baseline matches the model's separate-index operator chain
(including runtime Q/K `1 + weight`, two index contiguous operations,
two index Gemma RMSNorms, RoPE, and both cache-insertion calls). Timings
cover the complete prepare/cache region; no gather or copy is moved
outside measurement. Projection GEMMs and allocation are outside both
paths.

| Tokens | Baseline (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 32.73 | 3.07 | 10.67x |
| 4 | 37.40 | 3.45 | 10.85x |
| 8 | 41.71 | 3.66 | 11.41x |
| 16 | 50.96 | 4.55 | 11.20x |
| 32 | 59.96 | 6.66 | 9.01x |
| 64 | 64.47 | 8.48 | 7.60x |
| 128 | 67.47 | 11.34 | 5.95x |
| 192 | 76.05 | 14.40 | 5.28x |
| 256 | 86.53 | 17.50 | 4.95x |

At 192 tokens with 16/1/1 heads, latency is **82.92 -> 16.19 us** on
host 197 and **82.58 -> 15.95 us** on host 198. Independent host-198
repeat with 8/1/1 heads: **79.30 -> 14.15 us** at 192 tokens, **85.54 ->
17.20 us** at 256, and **104.93 -> 28.63 us** at 512. These are median
NPU Event timings in ACLGraph (20 captured calls, 10 replays, 5
samples). Separate eager profiler samples measured **20.56 us** for 16
heads on host 197 and **29.16 us** for 8 heads on host 198. An
additional same-run check measured 14.40 us with Event timing and
**21.22–21.36 us** for five graph replays inside the profiler. **The
profiler-based sub-20-us target is not met.** This is the fastest
numerically validated variant tested; sub-20-us holds only for the
unprofiled Event benchmark and does not establish service latency. The
fused region contains one kernel, with no separate gather, contiguous or
scatter. H20 latency was not measured here.

Latest validation on host 198 (A3, logical NPU 2, 2026-10-12) uses torch
2.10.0 + torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 / triton_ascend 3.2.2 (runtime
`triton.__version__` 3.2.0), and keeps `NUM_SLOTS` as a runtime scalar
with `do_not_specialize=["NUM_SLOTS"]`. This prevents both value and
alignment specialization. Head dimensions and layout strides
intentionally remain compile-time parameters.

```bash
pytest -q tests/ut/models/minimax_m3 \
  tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_minimax_qknorm_rope_cache.py
# 188 passed, 2 skipped (FP8 requires A5)
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/test_minimax_qknorm_rope_cache_performance.py \
  -o junit_family=legacy --junitxml=/tmp/minimax-qk-performance.xml
# 20 passed
```

The real compilation tests use an isolated real Triton JIT function and
count both dispatch-cache variants and calls into the real compilation
entry point:

- In one process, fixed BF16/layout: warm once, independently sweep
launch tokens (1/4/8/16/32/64/128/192/256/512), actual tokens
(`NUM_SLOTS`, including 0/1 and aligned/unaligned values), and cache
blocks (3/64/5392/8192). All **25 cases retain exactly one variant and
one compilation entry**. Cache writes also check that the runtime bound
actually changes.
- Nine distinct layouts each compile once (dense, main/index row
padding, strided positions, RoPE row padding, independent K/V/index
block padding, packed projections). Revisiting all nine with different
request sizes adds **zero variants or compilation entries**.
- Negative controls: restoring `tl.constexpr`, or removing
`do_not_specialize` alone, each makes the reuse test fail on a second
compiled variant. These controls ran in separate processes without
changing the production file.

The previous `benchmarks/minimax_qknorm_rope_cache.py` is removed.
Performance coverage is now a parametrized nightly e2e test. It
generates a constexpr reference from the same kernel body, checks
bit-exact outputs/cache writes, and alternates five timing samples (20
captured calls, 10 replays; compilation excluded). Tested 8/16 Q heads
and all ten token counts above with 5392 cache blocks. At 192 tokens:

| Q heads | constexpr NUM_SLOTS (us) | runtime NUM_SLOTS (us) | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 14.799 | 14.508 | -1.97% |
| 16 | 16.342 | 16.176 | -1.02% |

Across all 20 cases, changes ranged from -6.77% to +1.10%; no clear
regression was observed. Small differences are measurement variation,
not evidence that removing specialization intrinsically speeds up the
kernel. These are unprofiled NPU Event measurements on an otherwise idle
test card in a shared host, not service latency or profiler
measurements.

Correctness coverage includes guards/fallback, fake/dummy handling,
separate projections without concat, insertion ordering, CPU-reference
numerical comparisons, multiple head layouts, partial/full RoPE,
independent shuffled/negative slots, untouched cache regions,
non-contiguous strides, empty inputs, graph replay after positions/slots
changes, and dynamic cache capacity. Runtime JIT reuse does not imply
that ACLGraph buckets or captured scalar arguments update automatically.

`bash format.sh ci` was run. Ruff, formatting, spelling, Markdown,
workflow and Python checks pass except the pre-existing missing
`ops/triton/msa/__init__.py` (deliberately owned by #18294). Windows
cannot execute the Linux-only gitleaks/logger hooks and lacks
shellcheck; logger and shellcheck passed separately on Linux, and
gitleaks passed for the changed files. No claim that the full check
suite is green until the package-init dependency is resolved.

New raw compile-count, negative-control, correctness and performance
logs (including JUnit timing properties):
`/home/codex-minimax-kv192-20261011/constexpr-20261012/` on host 198.
Earlier full-chain baseline/profiler results above are historical
measurements from the initial fusion implementation.

**PD validation limit:** attempted real W8A8 1P1D on hosts 197/198
following tutorial section 5.3: P DP2/TP4/PP2 with FlashComm1, D
DP4/TP4/PP1 with ACLGraph, EP and EAGLE3. All four D APIs became healthy
and were reachable cross-host. P failed during Mooncake Ascend Direct
initialization with `EI0009: The network port is down`, followed by
TransferEngine initialization failure and worker exit. Host `hccn_tool`
confirmed DOWN links. No successful PD request, end-to-end accuracy or
throughput is claimed. Operator validation is the explicitly requested
fallback; keep this PR draft pending service validation. A5/FP8 remains
unverified.

Implementation details and reproduction:
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/minimax_qknorm_rope_cache.md`. Raw
operator, correctness, profiler and service artifacts:
`/home/codex-minimax-kv192-20261011/` on both test hosts.

AI-assisted workflow: inspected CUDA/Ascend references, compared
parallel and grouped-vector variants on A3, added dynamic-cache and
graph-replay tests, and attempted real-weight PD deployment.

old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The DeepSeek V4.1 guide still says support requires `main` and does not
list the 1017 checkpoints. Update the v0.30.0rc2 documentation to state
that the release supports both DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, link the official [Hugging Face 1017
checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017),
and add a link for Ascend users to
[Eco-Tech/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w8a8](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w8a8).

Preserve the existing official and Ascend W8A8 model links and add the
1017 links alongside them. Synchronize the corresponding Chinese
translation entries. Keep the deployment commands unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No runtime or API changes. Documentation only.

### How was this patch tested?

- Verified the official Hugging Face repository and `config.json`:
`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` / `deepseek_v41`; the official checkpoint
declares FP8 quantization with FP4 experts.
- Verified the ModelScope repository metadata and file-list API. At
verification time, its file list contained README/configuration files;
weight shards were not yet listed. The guide therefore references the
repository without asserting that the upload is complete.
- `pre-commit run markdownlint --hook-stage manual --files
docs/source/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.md` passed.
- Validated PO quoted-string syntax, all three new English paragraph IDs
against the source document, matching translated URLs, and no newly
introduced duplicate IDs.
- `git diff origin/releases/v0.30.0rc2 --check` passed.
- Attempted `bash format.sh ci`; stopped the run while it was stalled
installing the `actionlint` environment. Full-repository formatting was
not completed locally.

No inference code changes; no new runtime tests were added.
